Investing time, knowledge and experience is necessary in order to build a story that we can believe in and stand behind with our joint efforts. That's why, as much as the performances convey a message to children and young people all over Croatia about the importance of recognizing true values ​​in life, such as free time, responsible money management and lifelong learning, we also revive the entrepreneurial spirit through our own involvement and preparations for each performance. A performance, although a product, is a living organism whose main characteristic is relationship because it exists and develops through interaction with others. 

Deepening the understanding of the responsibility of dramatic expression in the function of teaching, and in our case primarily financial literacy, resulted in an interesting process that grows and develops from performance to performance."

articles.title: Prof. Ph.D. Stjepan Orešković in Osijek: "If you think knowledge is expensive, try ignorance"
articles.description: Prof. Ph.D. Stjepan Orešković to young people in Osijek: "If you think education is expensive, try ignorance"
articles.excerpt: Prof. Ph.D. Stjepan Orešković to young people in Osijek: "If you think education is expensive, try ignorance"
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
While many still measure their success mainly by income or titles, prof. Ph.D. Stjepan Orešković has been emphasizing something far more valuable for years - knowledge, character and humanity.

One of the most successful Croatian entrepreneurs, the founder and majority owner of the BOSQAR Group, gave an inspiring lecture to young people in Osijek yesterday, which is still talked about today. The biggest cost, says prof. Orešković, it is not education, but ignorance!

With the lecture "When ignorance becomes too expensive", held on June 9 at the Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences in Osijek, in front of about 90 students and professors of the Gaudeamus High School and the Osijek School of Economics, prof. Orešković showed once again why entrepreneurship is not only a matter of business results, but above all a way of thinking and readiness for continuous personal development.

The meeting was organized in cooperation with the Biti Bolji Association and the Poduzetnik magazine, which was the media sponsor of the event.

Powerful thoughts as the backbone of an inspiring lecture

In one of his interviews for the Poduzetnik magazine, Prof. Orešković quoted the former president of Harvard University Derek Bok: "If you think education is expensive, try ignorance!"

This powerful thought was the starting point of the lecture, which opened up a series of topics about learning, life values, success, resilience and happiness.

Speaking about happiness and success, prof. Orešković emphasized that the purpose of life is to be happy, but that happiness is not the absence of problems. On the contrary, true strength is found in developing resilience, the ability to face challenges and find solutions when circumstances are not ideal. Life will always bring obstacles, he said, and it is up to us to develop the skills and character necessary to overcome them.

He placed special emphasis on lifelong learning and personal development. According to him, if we want to change the world around us and help others, we must first invest in our own growth. Success is not measured exclusively by business results, functions or material achievements, but by the number of people on whom we have left a positive mark during our lives.

He also sent a strong message to young people about the importance of discipline. One of the biggest battles in life, he pointed out, is fought with oneself. It is precisely discipline, consistency and the willingness to choose what is best for us in the long term on a daily basis that create the foundations for personal and professional success.

At the end of the lecture, he referred to the importance of interpersonal relationships. He reminded that numerous studies confirm that people who nurture sincere, high-quality and stable relationships with others live the longest and best quality. This is another proof that true success is not only built through a career, but also through the people we are surrounded by.

The lecture managed to encourage young people to think about knowledge, responsibility, personal growth and values that bring the greatest return in the long run. Because investing in oneself, concluded prof. Orešković, is the only investment that never loses its value.

The show "Money" continues to combine education and the arts, bringing topics that are crucial for their future closer to young people in a way that is understandable, entertaining and inspiring. 

The play "Money" is already well known to audiences throughout Croatia. It is a witty, educational and somewhat provocative piece of theater that in an accessible way opens important topics of financial literacy, as well as the relationship to time, work and personal values. So far, about 4,500 viewers of different generations have seen the play, which confirms its relevance and strong connection with the public. 

Thanks to the well-coordinated acting duo, Monika Duvnjak and Gabriel Perić, who convey the play's messages with ease and conviction, the project is successfully developing this year as well through a series of planned performances, and several more performances are scheduled for the end of the school year.

Through play, music and vivid stage situations, the play encourages viewers to think about how we make decisions about money and time and how these decisions shape our daily lives. It was such meetings filled with learning, laughter and interaction that resulted in a simple but powerful message: money should be used as a tool for personal growth and creating a better society.

articles.title: Entrepreneurship without a filter: Lessons that remain
articles.description: The "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project has been confirming for the thirteenth year how important it is to bring the real world of entrepreneurship closer to young people.
articles.excerpt: The "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project has been confirming for the thirteenth year how important it is to bring the real world of entrepreneurship closer to young people.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Manuel Šola at the Bjelovar Technical School
articles.content:
Project "Biti Bolji - Be Better" for the thirteenth year, it confirms how important it is to bring the real world of entrepreneurship closer to young people - one that is not only learned from textbooks, but through experience, mistakes and personal growth.

Just such a meeting was held on April 8, 2026 at the Bjelovar Technical School, where she held a lecture for about forty students and ten professors. Manuel Šola, an entrepreneur whose professional journey has lasted for an impressive 27 years. Without embellishment and big promises, she showed the students a realistic picture of entrepreneurship, which includes a lot of work, risk and uncertainty, but also the freedom that comes with the opportunity to shape our own time and decisions. Recalling her own beginnings, she pointed out how much the business world has changed: technology that was once just in its infancy is now an indispensable tool, and the competition is stronger and more competent than ever before. However, the key decision remains the same – do we dare to go our own way. 

She placed a special emphasis on the importance of personality in business, especially in the area of communications she deals with. Although knowledge is more accessible today than ever, what makes the difference is not just the information, but how we apply it. This is exactly where soft skills come into play - skills that arise from our habits, character and attitude towards work and people. 

Speaking about young people, she pointed out that generation Z brings numerous advantages, strength in technology, responsibility and courage in working with numbers. However, it is equally important to develop resistance to stress and the ability to cope with the challenges brought by a dynamic business environment. "You were born at the best time," she said, emphasizing the opportunities that today's world offers. She also touched on the ever-present role of artificial intelligence in communication and everyday life, encouraging students to continuously develop their own knowledge, which they will be able to improve further with the help of new technologies, as well as manage their time smarter.

The lecture soon turned into an open and interactive conversation, filled with numerous questions from students who showed sincere interest and desire to learn. In the end, the message she left behind was simple but powerful: "Find what you love and what you want to do, because that's where the key to happiness and success lies."

Meetings like this remind us that the greatest lessons are often those that come from real life - and that real inspiration begins when someone decides to share their experience with others.

articles.title: First-hand inspiration: entrepreneurship with integrity
articles.description: The "Biti Bolji – Be Better" project has successfully brought together students and entrepreneurship from practice for the thirteenth year.
articles.excerpt: The "Biti Bolji – Be Better" project has successfully brought together students and entrepreneurship from practice for the thirteenth year.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Niko Tokić Kartelo at the Isidor Kršnjavog Secondary School in Našice
articles.content:
In Našice and Donji Miholjec - a meeting that leaves a mark

In a time when quick successes and shortcuts are often sought, the students of Isidor Kršnjavog High School in Našice and Donji Miholjac High School, a total of 310 students - 230 of them from Našice and 80 from Donji Miholjac - had the opportunity to hear a story that restores faith in authenticity, effort and consistency. He was a guest at these schools on March 10, 2026 Niko Tokić Kartelo, as part of the "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project, which has been successfully implemented in cooperation with schools for the thirteenth year. 

Without embellishment and big phrases, through lines from his own life, he brought the students closer to what it really means to be an entrepreneur. He spoke about challenges, mistakes, but also about the importance of honesty, integrity and responsibility in business - values ​​that, although sometimes neglected, make a difference in the long run. 

His simple and direct communication style created an atmosphere where students felt free to ask questions, think aloud, and connect their dreams with real possibilities. The lecture was followed by just such an open dialogue - a series of questions, gifts, photography and conversations that showed how important this kind of meeting is to the students.

There were no shortage of reactions - students and professors from both schools unanimously pointed out that the lecture was extremely interesting, meaningful and, above all, inspiring. Because sometimes hearing one honest story is enough to start a new one of your own in the future.

Inspirational lecture in Đakovo

In the school library of the "Braća Radić" School of Economics, Đakovo, where on March 13, 2026 an additional place was sought, about a hundred students welcomed the lecture with great interest Maje Ilčić, an entrepreneur whose approach combines life practice and education.

Through an authentic story called "We are not robots", she brought the students closer to the importance of understanding their own body and attitude towards nutrition. Without complicated theories, she talked about the basics that make the difference: what kind of food we choose, what a caloric surplus and deficit means, and how our body functions even while we are at rest, through basal metabolism. 

The emphasis was clear: there is no universal solution, but there is a need for balance. The special value of the lecture was given by a personal touch - Maja's own example confirmed that changes are not reserved for "someone else", but are very much attainable by anyone who decides to listen to their body.

The meeting concluded with questions, taking photos and, perhaps most importantly, small promises to yourself that you will take a step towards healthier choices. Because, as the students had the opportunity to hear - we are not robots, but we can learn to take care of ourselves in the right way.

articles.title: Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas: from classroom to real business experience
articles.description: The project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" at the Third School of Economics in Zagreb continued with the final presentations of the students, which rounded off the process...
articles.excerpt: The project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" at the Third School of Economics in Zagreb continued with the final presentations of the students, which rounded off the process...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: At the Third School of Economics in Zagreb, the final presentations of student teams were held on March 17, 2026.
articles.content:
Project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" in Third School of Economics Zagreb it continued with the final presentations of the students on March 17, 2026, which rounded off the process that began in mid-February with the introductory lecture "Entrepreneurial START".

During a month of work, the students developed their own business ideas and prepared them for presentation in front of an expert jury. The final event was attended by about forty students, including those who did not participate in the project, which confirms the great interest in entrepreneurial topics among young people. A total of 19 students, including one student with special needs with the support of an assistant, presented their projects through four teams: Energo Napitak, Stolarija Knež, Ideon and Shadesync.

The expert jury consisted of Vladimir Mihajlović - director and editor-in-chief of the Poduzetnik magazine, project coordinator at the school of prof. Julija Schwaiberger, prof. Mirela Šivak Poklečki, Katarina Gudec - owner of the company BORDO Primo and Lara Levak from the company Grizli komunikacije. 

The students were evaluated according to the originality of the idea and the brand, the completeness and feasibility of the concept, the way of presentation and teamwork, with special emphasis on the quality of market research as the basis of every business decision.

Each team showed a high level of engagement and understanding of the process - from market analysis to the formulation of a specific offer. After the presentations, the students received concrete advice and questions that helped them to further see the strengths and possibilities of improving their projects.

The victory was taken by the Shadesync team, which consisted of Ana Prša, Larisa Tomić, Margareta Pintarić and Leona Majić. Although the jury had a divided opinion, especially emphasizing the quality of the Ideon team's analysis, the creativity and clarity of the winning team's presentation were the deciding factors. Some students of the winning team also participate in the teaching program "Trainee companies" and "Entrepreneurship", showing how important the connection between theory and practice is in the development of young entrepreneurs.

As a reward, the students visited the company on March 26 Grizzly Communications, where they had the opportunity to get to know the real business environment. With the guidance of Lara Levak, they learned about work processes in the agency, the division of tasks and key activities in communication with clients. Through conversation and interactive questions, such as thinking about their own future career or selecting relevant news, they further developed critical thinking and communication skills.

This project once again confirmed its value - the students not only gained knowledge, but also experience, security and an entrepreneurial way of thinking, which will be the basis for future challenges.

articles.title: Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas: from an idea to a project in practice
articles.description: The project "Biti Bolji - 1000 ideas" was successfully concluded at Ban Josip Jelačić - Zaprešić Secondary School, which enabled students to...
articles.excerpt: The project "Biti Bolji - 1000 ideas" was successfully concluded at Ban Josip Jelačić - Zaprešić Secondary School, which enabled students to...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: In Ban Josip Jelačić - Zaprešić Secondary School, the final presentations were held on March 18, 2026.
articles.content:
The project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" was successfully concluded in Secondary school Ban Josip Jelačić - Zaprešić, which provided economic students with a unique learning experience through practice - from the first business idea to a concrete project application.

The final presentations were held on March 18, 2026, with the participation of 24 students. Under the mentorship of professor Monika Škalec, students worked in five teams: ReforMe, Cakery, JTL Sports, 3D Print Studio and Aroma. Each team presented their own company and a simulation of the application to the real competition for the allocation of incentives from EU funds for the Zagreb County in 2025. 

The task was not easy - the students had to take into account all the key elements of the project proposal, from formal conditions such as the date of establishment of the company, headquarters and number of employees, to financial projections and the requested amount of support. It was this approach that allowed them to understand how much attention needs to be paid to every detail in order for the project to be successful.

The students found inspiration for their ideas in their own environment and interests - from sports activities and the needs of the local community, which resulted in the JTL Sports project, to the upgrading of existing family entrepreneurial stories like ReforMe, but also completely new and creative concepts.

The works were evaluated by an expert jury consisting of: Jurja Horvat - director of the company Bandiera d.o.o., Vladimir Mihajlović - director and editor-in-chief of the magazine Poduzetnik, prof. Anita Kola Brundić, project mentor - Prof. Monika Škalec and Katarina Gudec - owner of the company BORDO Primo. After each presentation, the students received concrete and expert feedback, with an emphasis on the details that make the difference between a good and a successful project application. 

The victory was almost unanimously won by the Cakery team, which consisted of Tessa Gluhačić, Mia Rinčić, Lorena Taboršak, Marija Jakšić and Anamarija Piljanović. Their project stood out for its precision, clarity and creative approach, with attention paid to every segment - from the development of the idea to the application itself.

As a reward, the winning team visited the company on March 25 Bandiera d.o.o., where the students had the opportunity to see firsthand what working with clients on real projects looks like. During the two-hour meeting, they got acquainted with content creation processes, working in the WordPress interface, and tried their hand at using podcast recording equipment, further expanding their practical skills.

The project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" confirmed the importance of experiential learning and connecting education with the real sector, and provided students with valuable experience that prepares them for further education and the challenges of the labor market.

articles.title: Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas: Entrepreneurial START
articles.description: As part of the "Biti Bolji - 1000 ideas" project, a lecture was held at the Third School of Economics in Zagreb and the launch of a task called "Entrepreneurial START".
articles.excerpt: As part of the "Biti Bolji - 1000 ideas" project, a lecture was held at the Third School of Economics in Zagreb and the launch of a task called "Entrepreneurial START".
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Students in the Biti Bolji-1000 idea project
articles.content:
As part of the "Biti Bolji - 1000 ideas" project, on February 17, 2026, a lecture was held at the Third School of Economics in Zagreb and the launch of a task called "Entrepreneurial START".

She was a guest lecturer Katarina Gudec from the company BORDO Primo, and the meeting was realized in cooperation with the professor Julia Schwaiberger, project coordinator at this school. 17 students out of a total of 20 participated, including one student with special needs and his assistant. 

The goal of the project is to develop an entrepreneurial and creative way of thinking in students through experiential learning. The emphasis is on the students, using a specific example, to go through the entire process of starting a business idea - from the first idea to reaching clients, with minimal financial investments and a strong focus on content and organic visibility. The project encourages them to think like brand owners, take responsibility and make strategic decisions. 

The task is for students in teams of three to four members to create their own brand from scratch within 30 days. They define the name, visual identity and communication, research the market through surveys and interviews, analyze the competition using the SWOT model and shape a unique offer. They lay the marketing foundations through the 4P model, create a promotion and sales plan and prepare three types of ads – educational, inspirational and sales – based on the real words of their potential clients.

Special emphasis is placed on the understanding process: from research and strategy to visibility and first clients. Students learn how to turn an idea into a viable concept, how to clearly communicate the value of a product or service, and how to make decisions together and collaborate effectively. Each team has defined leadership roles, a marketing person and a finance person, but all members participate in key decisions, developing a sense of ownership and responsibility. 

The final presentation is scheduled for March 17, 2026, when the teams will present their brand and overall development strategy. The commission will select the most successful team based on originality, elaboration of the concept and quality of team cooperation. The winners will have the opportunity to visit the marketing agency and get to know the actual work process - from idea to campaign.

The expected effect of the project is clear: students understand how the market works, acquire concrete foundations for starting a business, and develop self-confidence and an entrepreneurial spirit that goes beyond the classroom.

articles.title: The simple way of communication left a strong impression on everyone present
articles.description: Successful entrepreneur Niko Tokić Kartelo visited the students of the "Braća Radić" School of Economics in Đakovo and the Gaudeamus Gymnasium in Osijek.
articles.excerpt: Successful entrepreneur Niko Tokić Kartelo visited the students of the "Braća Radić" School of Economics in Đakovo and the Gaudeamus Gymnasium in Osijek.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Teaching at the "Braća Radić" School of Economics in Đakovo
articles.content:
As part of the "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project, which has been implemented in cooperation with schools for twelve years in a row, 70 students of the "Braća Radić" School of Economics in Đakovo and 35 students of the Gaudeamus High School in Osijek visited on November 11, 2025 Niko Tokić Kartelo, a successful Croatian entrepreneur, lecturer and motivational speaker known for his authentic approach to business and life. 

The lecture in both schools was extremely interesting, meaningful and instructive, as confirmed by the students and professors of these schools, who enthusiastically participated in the conversation. In a practical way, with lines from his private life, he brought the students closer to what it means to be an entrepreneur and how to do business honestly and with integrity in today's world. His honest and simple way of communication left a strong impression on everyone present.

After the lecture, Mr. Tokić Kartelo was happy to answer numerous questions from the students in both schools, and took photos with them, leaving behind inspiration and motivation for future challenges. 

One of the moments that particularly touched the students was when Mr. Tokić gave a Hajduk jersey to the students Sara Crnoja from the Djakovac school. 

In her thanks, Sara wrote:

"Dear Mr. Tokić Kartelo,

I would like to thank you for an extremely interesting and pleasant lecture. It was very pleasant to listen to you, and I especially appreciate the way you encouraged young people to think about the importance of giving. A big thank you for the gift, the Hajduk jersey. It really means a lot to me, not only as a cheerleader, but also as a memory of an inspiring lecture. When I received it, it was so special to me that I could only say: "Mom, I did it." Best regards, Sara Crnoja, 4.UR"

Mr. Niko repeated the same gesture of donating a jersey, but this time to NK Osijek, in the Gaudeamus Gymnasium, where he once again caused particularly emotional moments that the students will remember and retell among themselves for a long time. 

This meeting between entrepreneurs and students once again confirmed the importance of the "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project, which provides students with the opportunity to learn directly from successful people and learn about the values of hard work, ethics and personal growth.

We believe that such lectures are especially useful for young people who are already thinking that one day they will enter the entrepreneurial waters by starting their own business, and we sincerely look forward to the next meetings of students with new guests in schools.

articles.title: Pupils' visit to the factory in Nova Gradiška
articles.description: About fifty high school students from Osijek and Vinkovci visited the Klimaoprema company as part of the Biti Bolji - Be Better project.
articles.excerpt: About fifty high school students from Osijek and Vinkovci visited the Klimaoprema company as part of the Biti Bolji - Be Better project.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: High school students from Osijek and Vinkovci visiting Klimaoprema d.d.
articles.content:
As part of the Biti Bolji - Be Better project, which has been inspiring and encouraging young people to learn about the world of entrepreneurship for more than ten years, on November 4, 2025, about fifty high school students from Osijek and Vinkovci visited the company Klimaoprema d.d. 

The students were welcomed by the President of the Management Board Sergio Galosic, with a story about his own beginnings, about the days when he himself was a student and about his first steps in Klimaoprema. 

Representatives of the company took the students, accompanied by a professor, through the plant in Nova Gradiška, seeing how the production process goes from idea to finished product. The students learned how the parts that make up clean spaces and ventilation systems are made, but also felt the atmosphere of cooperation that drives everything. 

Klimaoprema says that meetings like this are important because each generation brings new energy, and they welcome these new young people with open doors, stressing that the future of the industry depends on them.

"At Klimaoprema, we love when the plant comes alive with young faces, curious looks and questions."

Students' review of this visit

"During the tour of the Klimaoprema factory, we had the opportunity to learn about modern production processes and the organization of work in one of the leading companies in the field of ventilation and air conditioning systems. The tour began in the production plant, where we could see how various elements of ventilation systems are created - from the production of metal parts, bending and joining, to final quality control. The workers use modern machines and technology, and it is evident that great attention is paid to precision and safety in their work. The tour enabled us to better understand the entire production process and the importance of teamwork and technical knowledge in the air conditioning industry. We then visited the warehouse where we saw a precisely organized system of receiving, storing and distributing materials. We were particularly impressed by the automation and order in which everything takes place, which enables the efficient flow of goods and the rapid preparation of components for production. The tour enabled us to better understand the importance of teamwork and technical knowledge in the air conditioning industry." (Jana Vučković and Laura Vuković, 3rd grade; Ruđer Bošković Technical School and Science High School, Osijek) 

"This was a unique opportunity to see and get to know how parts for ventilation units are produced. From the raw material, which is sheet metal wound into large coils, weighing several tons, to the final product, which is packaged and distributed to the end consumer." (Antonio Bjezancevic, 2nd year; Ruđer Bošković Technical School and Science High School, Osijek)

articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović

articles.content:
Project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" once again confirmed how important it is to enable young people to learn through real experiences and a direct encounter with entrepreneurial practice. Through this pilot project, students School of Applied Art and Design Osijek they had the opportunity to develop their own ideas, learn about branding and design, and get to know the entire process of product creation - from idea to market.

The project has started October 31, 2025. by a lecture by an entrepreneur Janje Pavetic from the company MagisWall, which introduced the MagisWall and LittleSari brands, their business philosophy, visual identity and development path to the students. Special emphasis is placed on entrepreneurship, the importance of perseverance, product quality and clear market communication. On that occasion, the students were presented with the main task – to design their own brand of children's beanbags within 30 days.

Working in teams, students developed complete brands – from name and visual identity, through product design, to promotional and sales strategy. The final presentations were held December 5, 2025. at the Osijek School of Applied Art and Design, where students presented five original brands: MOLLIS, XOLO, SORV, HALO Company and MONDO.

The judging panel, made up of experts from the fields of design, entrepreneurship and communications, declared the winning team HALO Company, with the emphasis that all presented projects showed an exceptional level of creativity, thoughtfulness and teamwork.

A visit to MagisWall – an experience that lasts

The highlight of the project was visit to the MagisWall company in Zagreb, December 12, 2025., when it is nine students and five mentor professors, accompanied by the organizers - members of the Biti Bolji Association, had the opportunity to get to know the real business and production process. During this visit, the students were introduced to the final products, participated in an educational quiz and listened to a strong and sincere motivational speech about the importance of endurance in difficult times and not giving up on your dreams. 

Tour showroom and production plant it gave them insight into the entire process of creating wallpaper - from designing the design, technological preparation and printing, to installing it on the wall. A special impression was left by the story of the beginnings of the company 15 years ago, when enthusiasm and vision were the key drivers of development, as well as today's image of MagisWall, which has the most modern machines at its disposal.

The students were particularly impressed by i exhibition space in the Family Mall, where they could see how a creative idea becomes a professionally designed, marketable product.

A joint lunch was organized for all participants, which additionally contributed to the pleasant atmosphere and exchange of impressions, after which the return to Osijek followed. 

The day passed in an exceptional atmosphere - all participants positively express their satisfaction with being in a creative environment, while the students, full of inspiration and new ideas, returned to their homes. The visit was rounded off in the holiday spirit - the students received Christmas presents from the company MagisWall, and one special gift, which is Janja Pavetic intended for the school, he symbolically emphasized the importance of continuous encouragement of creativity and creativity among young people.

Project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" once again showed how connecting education and entrepreneurship creates a strong foundation for the development of young people, providing them not only with knowledge, but also real experience, inspiration and faith in one's own abilities.

The members of the Biti Bolji Association sincerely thank you Janja and Dražen Pavetić and the team MagisWall on the openness, hospitality and mentoring that significantly contributed to the quality and successful implementation of the project, as well as on the partnership cooperation that made this project a real, inspiring and unforgettable experience for the students.

articles.title: Students of the Osijek School of Applied Art and Design developed their own brands as part of the project "Biti Bolji - 1000 ideas"
articles.description: A successful cycle of the educational project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" was held at the Osijek School of Applied Art and Design, which...
articles.excerpt: A successful cycle of the educational project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" was held at the Osijek School of Applied Art and Design, which...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Participants of the project "Biti Bolji - 1000 ideas"
articles.content:
A successful cycle of the educational project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" was held at the Osijek School of Applied Arts and Design, which offers young people the opportunity to prove themselves in creating their own product and brand.

An introduction to the world of branding and entrepreneurship

In the first part of the project, on October 31, 2025, the students got to know the brands MagisWall i LittleSari, their history, philosophy and development of visual identity. Entrepreneur Janja Pavetic she spoke about the challenges and responsibilities of entrepreneurship, explaining what makes a quality product, how a brand develops and what are the basics of market communication.

The lecture was also a preparation for the students' main task – making their own brand of children's beanbags.

Task: Create your own brand in 30 days

The students worked in teams of five or six members, and the goal was to design a brand of children's bean bags. They had to create:

  • brand name and visual identity,
  • product line with unique models,
  • promotion and sales plan and define the target market and communication channels.

The emphasis was on creativity, playfulness and originality, but also on the realistic possibility of placing the product on the market.

Learning through practice

Project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" is designed as an experiential workshop that reveals the full process of product development to students. From the first idea, through design and branding, all the way to presentation and positioning on the market, young people participated in every step - just like real entrepreneurs.

The goal was to encourage them to an entrepreneurial way of thinking, but also to show what a realistic creative process looks like when it is necessary to combine aesthetics, functionality and market logic.

Final presentations and presented brands

At the final presentation, on December 5, 2025, each team presented their brand through a 10 to 15-minute presentation. The students prepared a brand story, a brand logo, product sketches and prototypes, promotional materials and a marketing strategy.

• Five brands were presented:

1. MOLLIS (Iva Šnajder, Lucija Bandov, Antonio Marković, Duje Buljubasic, Dora Babić)

2. XOLO (Mia Manojlović, Josipa Kovačević, Mila Radošević, David Konjarević, Larisa Nikolić, Ivona Marton)

3. SORV (Vanessa Burcar, Katarina Sabljak, Dona Ocelić, Sara Kožić, Lucija Bukovčak, Teodor Vranješević

4. HALO Company (Luka Radat, Tea Marček, Karla Karić, Andreja Bertić, Leonarda Franjić)

5. MONDO (Andrijana Radočaj, Gita Rudež, Lucija Miletić, Lucija Barukčić, Snježana Stubičan)

Professors Ančica Liović, Lidija Terzić and Anamarija Barba took on the role of mentors, while the project was coordinated by the Association Biti Bolji – Vladimir Mihajlović and Marica Vrkljan.

Choosing the best idea

The judging panel, consisting of: Janja Pavetić, Dražen Pavetić, Mirjana Felinger, Marija Adrić Soldo and Josip Kaniža, evaluated the works according to the criteria of originality, visual quality, innovation, implementation of the concept and the quality of the team presentation. After reviewing the presentations, the commission declared HALO Company the winning team. However, due to the extremely high quality and originality of all the works, it was decided that on December 12, one representative from the remaining four teams will go to Zagreb for the final visit to the MagisWall company.

A visit to MagisWall – a first-hand experience

On December 12, 2025, students, together with professors and project coordinators, will visit the MagisWall facility, where they will be able to see the actual development and production process – from idea to finished product. Meeting with designers, technologists and the MagisWall team will be a valuable opportunity to deepen new knowledge and understand how a creative idea turns into a tangible product.

Acknowledgment and announcement of the continuation of the project

The project once again confirmed how important it is to provide students with practical experiences and real challenges.

"Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" will continue to open space for the development of ideas, learning and cooperation with the real sector to young creatives in the coming generations.

articles.title: You must always do your best in everything you do!
articles.description: As part of the "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project, a lecture was held for students of the Osijek School of Economics and Administration, where Kristijan Ilovača was a guest.
articles.excerpt: As part of the "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project, a lecture was held for students of the Osijek School of Economics and Administration, where Kristijan Ilovača was a guest.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Kristijan Ilovača at the Osijek School of Economics and Administration
articles.content:
As part of the project "Biti Bolji - Be Better" On October 9, 2025, an inspiring lecture was held for 35 students of the Osijek School of Economics and Administration. He was a guest Kristijan Ilovača, a young successful entrepreneur who arrived from Africa the night before, and the very next morning - without rest - came to his former school. His life's mission, he said, is to inspire young people.

Meeting with students and the principal Lidija Žaper, his former professor, he was extremely emotional.

"I looked at the school building for a long time before I entered," said Kristijan, recalling his school days as tears welled up in his eyes. His story of perseverance, discipline and personal growth resonated strongly with the students. 

He honestly admitted that after high school he didn't finish the college he went to, but today he has three degrees. He was a member of the Cohort, trained in kickboxing, and found inspiration in the special forces - from them, he says, he unknowingly took over military discipline. At the age of 25, he left for the USA, where he started all over again.

"I realized that I didn't know anything, so I studied and worked on myself every day."

Three years later, he applied to the FBI Academy, which, he says, completely changed his life. 

"You must always do your best when you do something, because there is a thin line between success and failure," he told the students. He advised them not to be afraid of challenges, to learn, explore and develop their skills.

"Time passes quickly - do sports, hobbies, discover what moves you. I didn't know I was an entrepreneur until I became one."

Today, he runs his own company and organizes Security and Defense Fair, which grew into a successful event.

He told the students: "Be good people. You have time to correct your mistakes, but never give up on your dreams. If you have fire and a spark in your eyes, you can achieve anything."

NOVAC performance in Našice

In the Isidor Kršnjavog High School - Našice, on October 31, 2025, the play was performed twice on the same day in the morning and afternoon shifts, and a total of 357 first and second grade students watched it. Gabriel Perić, an actor in the play Novac, who is also part of the author's team, gave his review of this guest appearance.

"There is something special in the fact that I have already performed at the Isidor Kršnjavog High School in Našice as a high school student at the county level of LiDraN even twice and that now as a professional actor-puppeteer I have returned to the same place where I almost started my theatrical journey with planks that mean life. Collection and activity proposal for Magis Walla's new brand called LittleSari (children's products). Put them in the role of driving that brand, which is all they need to do.

articles.title: Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas
articles.description: The project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" is intended for young people who know what they want to be or are still exploring what they would like to become.
articles.excerpt: The project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" is intended for young people who know what they want to be or are still exploring what they would like to become.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
A new project that should encourage high school students to think creatively, develop concrete ideas and create new products and services in order to strengthen awareness of the importance of production and entrepreneurship in Croatian society.

Project "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas" it is intended for young people who know what they want to be or are still exploring what they would like to become. Let's help young people to bring to light their characteristics, potentials, preferences, but also their shortcomings. Let them learn how to emphasize what they should, or soften what they shouldn't. We want to help them discover their hidden talents and skills, guide them in acquiring the competencies needed for entrepreneurship, as well as how to deal with the challenges of the market, how to find themselves in all of this. We want to prepare them well for their own job, for college or for the job market after high school. With this project, young people will get answers to questions about how to jump over barriers and overcome fear, how to do what we love and/or how to learn to love what we do.

The project holder is the Association Biti Bolji from Osijek, and the media sponsor is the magazine Poduzetnik.

Become part of a project that restores faith in young people, in ideas and in the possibility of something big starting from a small classroom! Give support to young and talented people who will be the bearers of economic development, employment of new generations, strengthening of environmental awareness and moral principles.

Description of the project

The project is implemented in secondary schools throughout Croatia with the aim of connecting students with the concepts of creating added value through entrepreneurship and the realization of their own ideas.

Students, with mentorship and support, come up with an idea for a new product, service or brand – with an emphasis on utility for small producers or the local community. Work will be done in teams, and the ideas will be presented in front of a committee that will select the three best teams. The project includes workshops, visits, teamwork and a final presentation. The focus is on creativity, production and ideas that bring together young people, entrepreneurs and the community.

Imagine a classroom where students not only learn about entrepreneurship, but become drivers of real change. A place where ideas come out of notebooks and become life-changing products, services and brands. That's exactly it "Biti Bolji – 1000 ideas", a project that brings together high schools, local producers and students in a common goal - creating concrete, useful and marketable solutions.

What are we doing?

We connect students with local manufacturing companies, craftsmen, the local and wider business community and the wider social community, who become activity holders/partners in the school. Through several practical workshops, mentoring meetings and visits to the factory/plant/place of work - students in teams develop their own idea for a new product or service. The best ideas will be awarded and presented to the general public, and sometimes realized in cooperation with the company.

Project activities

– Workshop 1 – The path from idea to market: presentation of the importance of production, the process of creative creation, development of a task for students (2 x 45 min).

– Workshop 2 – Final of ideas: presentation of works, selection of winners, awarding of prizes, inspirational story of each team (2 x 45 min).

– Visit to the production company – An insight into the real world of production for the winning team and transfer of experiences to schoolmates.

– Visibility and promotion - Media sponsor, stories of students, campaign "Small idea - Big effect" in cooperation with local media and schools.

Who are we looking for?

📍 Schools - who want to provide students with the experience of creation, teamwork and idea development.
📍 Poduzetnike and companies - who want to be the bearers of activities and mentor students.
📍 Donors and sponsors - who can financially support the project, prize fund or co-finance visits and realization of ideas.
📍 Local administration and community - which wants to invest in young people and support local creativity.

Why get involved?

Because the ideas we encourage today can employ people tomorrow, start production, keep young people in the community. Because we want to give schools new tools, young people a wind at their backs, and entrepreneurs a new perspective - through the eyes of students who think freely and create boldly.

articles.title: Children and artificial intelligence: My "friend" ChatGPT
articles.description: One of the most popular AI tools today is ChatGPT. Students use it to generate content or provide additional clarification tailored to them.
articles.excerpt: One of the most popular AI tools today is ChatGPT. Students use it to generate content or provide additional clarification tailored to them.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Jelena Đekić, collaboration of Gaudeamus High School in the project Biti Bolji-Be Better
articles.content:
One of the most popular AI tools today is ChatGPT. Students use it to generate content or provide additional clarification tailored to their learning style. 

However, in addition to the educational role, ChatGPT increasingly becomes a kind of "friend" for both adults and children - which raises important questions about the development of real relationships in the digital age. How does the development of artificial intelligence affect the development of emotional intelligence in children?

Through relationships with peers in the period of primary and secondary school, adolescents develop a sense of their own identity, learn to express their views, make decisions and stand up for themselves. This period is particularly sensitive because young people are building a sense of who they are, what they want and how they fit into the world around them. And to build key life skills like self-confidence, the ability to deal with disagreements and different perspectives, they need real relationships with their peers.

How are they Gaudeamus Gymnasium, contribution to the community and the healthy development of children is a fundamental value, precisely because of the previously asked questions, in cooperation with Vladimir Mihajlović from the magazine Poduzetnik as part of the project Biti Bolji – Be Better, we visited Elementary school Blago Zadro in Vukovar. We were welcomed there by 17 students of the 6th, 7th and 8th grades, who signed up for the workshop themselves and participated in the activities with great interest.

Workshop on artificial intelligence at Primary School Blage Zadre in Vukovar

We started with a brief introduction to basic emotions, after which we focused on the topic of differences between emotional and artificial intelligence. The children showed an enviable knowledge of AI, and when asked if ChatGPT could be their real friend, most answered "no". However, a couple of "maybe" and "maybe" responses were heard, as well as some silence that indicated doubt. 

Students gave examples of where ChatGPT helped them by providing them with comfort, which made them feel better. To demonstrate the difference between the help of a tool and a real person, we simulated situations where we asked ChatGPT for help as we would ask a friend. Although his advice was useful, it also revealed certain limitations that the children were not aware of until then.

Additionally, we examined the characteristic of the tool aimed at consistent adaptation to the user's wishes, without expressing opposing opinions or giving constructive feedback, while there is no natural space for a conflict of opinions and the development of argumentation - which are key elements in forming an attitude and value system. Moreover, in an effort to please the user, the tool will sometimes offer incorrect information.

We ended the workshop with a game of passing the ball and answering various questions. With this, we showed how valuable it is to spend time with others, share laughter, emotions and energy - something that no AI tool can do.

In the end, we all agreed that although ChatGPT is useful, it cannot replace the emotional dynamics and presence of a friend or other person - which is the basis for the healthy psychosocial development of any child.

Thanks to the well-trained actors, who convincingly convey the message of the play "Money" to the audience, we are carefree continuing with the planned guest appearances in schools throughout Croatia, and in the past month alone, another 750 students have seen the play.

He gave his review Gabriel Perić, an extremely talented actor in the play Novac, who is also part of the author's team. And he especially emphasized: "When we love what we do, every day is a game, and every challenge is a new incentive. Let us all have successful learning!"

Performance in Križevci and Đakovo

We performed the play Novac on April 7th at the elementary school "Vladimir Nazor" in Križevci, and on April 8th at the Economic School "Braća Radić" in Đakovo. We had both performances in the hallway of the school, which can be very challenging from a performing point of view, because the hallways echo and every noise can transfer the audience's attention in different directions, especially when it comes to a large number of students (as was the case here) and changes of different shifts, departures and arrivals to school, movement of teachers and cleaners.

In these situations, it is necessary to be even stronger and more impressive in the stage expression in order to overcome the influence of all these circumstances. The actor must always be fully present on the stage and believe in what he is doing in order to reach the truthfulness of the acting and the immediacy that will encourage and maintain contact with the audience. This relationship is the most important aspect of every theatrical performance, and with these performances we have just shown how we are up to all challenges by fully mastering the space, always seeking direct contact. In the same way, it is important to clearly transfer the logical accents of each individual thought, so that the echo does not diminish them and thus exclude the audience from the performance. The songs especially suited us because they enabled us to break through the fourth wall of the theater by going into the audience, transforming the entire corridor into a space for acting.

I was particularly impressed by the performance in Đakovo where 346 students watched us, which is actually the whole school. They were literally from all sides and we had the opportunity to apply the experience gained in larger play areas even better to the overall satisfaction of the students and school staff present. The students thanked us from the bottom of their hearts for coming and for the performance that they will remember for a long time.

Performance in Varaždin and Dugi Selo

We performed the play Novac on April 24 at the Varaždin Economic School and at the Dugo Selo High School, and on that day about 285 students of various majors saw it. We were surprised by the approach of the teachers, who explained to us how they implement more and more interactive content, workshops and different forms of teaching innovation in their teaching, which enable better and higher quality learning, thus making students more open to the articulation of their own thoughts and emotions and ultimately developing critical thinking, which was visible in the level of concentration following the play. 

Theatrical play is a platform for thinking and connecting different segments of private and business life, when we talk about financial literacy and its daily application, and in the school space this undoubtedly means the overall development of personality - from the professional business level all the way to the basic human level that gives the individual the opportunity to fully realize himself. This is precisely what I consider significant: the implementation of play as a basic principle of learning should not be intended exclusively for kindergarten and preschool age and classroom teaching, but should also be represented throughout schooling and lifelong education.

Of course, there are differences in the levels and methods of application, but one should always aim for the student to understand the comprehensiveness of teaching programs outside the framework of the school and education system. This is exactly why I am glad that we managed to combine the literary-historical context of the development of money and culture with the game of a brother and sister who connect it all with imagination and skillful use of concepts, thus providing a solid foundation for new knowledge, showing how the application of knowledge in everyday life can be not only useful but also fun. I sincerely hope that more and more schools and educational institutions will keep up with this approach to learning, where art will go hand in hand with entrepreneurship and science, making a coherent whole that will show us how we must never lose the will, desire and enthusiasm for learning, discovery and play, which is the basic prerequisite for a successful and quality life.

articles.content:
Eighty students actively listened to a lecture on how inflation affects our money, what investment is and why it is necessary to invest, but also why it is wise to invest long-term, disciplined and diversified, how to reduce risks and achieve financial independence in life.

We started with our new project "Life without money - Financial literacy of young people". Thank you InterCapital Asset Management d.o.o. Zagreb and the lecturer Igor Vihnanek which is 12.11.2024. visited Osijek, Tino Ujević Primary School and Mladost Primary School. 

Thank you to the Principal Tin Ujević, Domagoj Šokicicu, on supporting additional education that will benefit the students of his school; as well as the English language teacher Marijeta Kvetek from Mladost Primary School, who opens new horizons to her students with great enthusiasm. We know how much good teachers mean in our lives.

How is it to teach 5th to 8th grade kids about investing and finance?

Igor Vihnanek conveyed his impressions like this: "One morning, the Genius team in Zagreb got into a car and drove to Osijek, where we had the honor of talking to about 80 students from the Tino Ujevića elementary schools and the Mladost elementary school. I'll tell you right away - the children see everything from a perspective that we adults wouldn't have remembered in a hundred years! Of course, we adapted the lecture to their age, but they surprise you with knowledge and phenomenal questions."

"What if I invest in something, and that store is not doing well, can I invest in another?" They are very smart and bright and from the very beginning they think in the direction of what we call diversification and risk management. Two fingers in the air all the time - we have to admit that the girls were in the lead.

Knowledge is power, and control over one's own finances is one of the most useful skills for any human being. We have a duty to pass on knowledge to children that will be of great use to them in the future, and at the same time we must make sure that they are presented with both positive and negative sides. The point of our lectures was to provide them with an understanding of the basic concepts in a way familiar to them and to explain how to do it all smartly and safely. What is inflation, why is it wise to invest in the long term, how to reduce risks... Without advertising products and services!"

articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Twelve student scholarships for children who grow up without adequate parental care was awarded by OTP banka as part of its "Different World" donation program. Scholarships amount 300 euros per month, that is, in total 3,600 euros per year, and will provide students with financial support throughout the duration of their studies, provided that they regularly fulfill their academic obligations.

Donation program "A different world"

The program is part of the bank's broader socially responsible activities, aimed at creating equal opportunities for children and young people who face numerous challenges, and includes four scholarships for freshmen, while eight are intended for students of higher years of undergraduate and graduate studies. The total value of scholarships awarded for this academic year 2024/2025. is 43,200 euros, while during the entire course of study the amount exceeds 173,000 euros.

"Children who grow up without proper parental care often face insurmountable obstacles. Our 'Different World' program is designed to provide them with the opportunity for education and empower them on their way to independence. We are convinced that investing in education has far-reaching effects - it not only changes the lives of individuals, but contributes to the development of their entire society. By awarding these scholarships, we send a message that we believe in their potential and want to be part of their successful future", he pointed out Balázs Békeffy, President of the Management Board of OTP banka.

"A different world" is a program designed in response to the fact that only a small number of young people from the alternative care system continue their education after high school. The scholarship holders are students of various fields of study, from economics, law, health to technical and mechanical studies.

Financial and moral support for young people

OTP banka nurtures the tradition of socially responsible business and support for the local community, especially through initiatives that promote education and development. Through various scholarship and donation programs, the bank allocated more than 1.2 million euros in the past fourteen years, thus financing projects in the fields of culture, education, environmental protection and sports.

The "Different World" program is another step in that direction, providing not only financial, but also moral support to young people in one of the most sensitive phases of life. Scholarship holders will thus have the opportunity to participate in the bank's employee mentoring program, which will additionally try to facilitate their transition from education to the professional world.

"OTP banka wishes our scholarship holders the best of luck in their future academic education, with the hope that we have at least made it a little easier and helped them. Through projects like this, we are trying to show that it really is possible to do otherwise, that there is a different bank that, through its efforts, creates the conditions to leave a different, better world to new generations.".

With this initiative, OTP banka continues to confirm its commitment to socially responsible business and creating opportunities for children and young people who dream of a better future.

articles.title: "Money in Croatian schools": We went on a tour of schools in Croatia
articles.description: In October 2024, we performed the play "Money" in five Croatian schools, and the reactions of students and teachers were excellent.
articles.excerpt: In October 2024, we performed the play "Money" in five Croatian schools, and the reactions of students and teachers were excellent.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.featuredImageAlt: Center for Education "Vinko Bek" from Zagreb
articles.content:
In October 2024, we performed the play "Money" at the Vinko Bek Education Center from Zagreb, two primary schools in Zadar County and two secondary schools in Split, and the reactions of students and teachers were: "The play is excellent. The play was great. You are great!"

Elementary school "Valentin Klarin" Preko and elementary school "Vladimir Nazor" Neviđane

A small tour of primary schools in Zadar County was marked by many children's smiles and joy. The playful relationship between brother and sister, in which the brother helps the sister to solve a math homework, particularly impressed them because, among other things, it is not unknown to them that their elders help them with their schoolwork, trying to turn learning into a game that enables them to better remember and apply the material in new circumstances, which ultimately develops creativity and encourages the sharpening of intelligence. The songs were additional drivers of a kind of interactivity, as the children sang the leitmotifs of the play, which will surely stay with them for a long time. In particular, the central song of the play about the use of money and its purpose stood out, which removes the idea of ​​money as a goal and instead lays the foundation for understanding money as a means of achieving goals.

Likewise, 186 students got an insight into the system of valuing time as another important currency that should be paid special attention to because there is no money that can compensate for lost time. This is precisely why the issue of free time is also of great importance and, essentially, an integral part of financial literacy education. The best of all is that the children were inspired to ask the teachers questions about terms and concepts unknown to them, which means that we were able to stimulate curiosity and the desire to learn with our theatrical play. Their big applause and the greetings they sent to us only confirm everything that has been said. It's nice to be able to share the joy of educational theater play, especially in smaller communities that don't often have the opportunity to see and experience theater.

Commercial and trade school Split and School of Economics and Administration Split

167 secondary school students in Split were able to understand more deeply the concepts of investment in culture as a driver of development and building of society in a spiritual and intellectual sense. The trip to Renaissance Italy and the Republic of Dubrovnik gave them an insight into how much literature, architecture and theater play a role in creating identity, which then provides an opportunity to increase capital through the exchange of knowledge, experiences and the creation of large tourist centers. The issue of war profiteering and the large machinery that wars bring with them is also an important item in understanding the misuse of money as a means of cultivating a civilized way of life. The professors praised the thoughtfully interwoven collage of literary and historical background with which we explained the need to create money and the ways in which money established itself as an indispensable factor in thinking about a modern democratic society.

In the same way, questions about gender equality were important to the students, which we opened by giving fragments of the evolutionary development of that thought. Time travelers Siri and Ori also opened up the possibilities of further development of money by talking about the pressing issues of digitization and artificial intelligence. It is precisely this topic that provides the most opportunities for analysis within the teaching of the economic group of subjects. The issues of savings and pocket money also received a good response from the audience, understanding the need for thoughtful disposal of assets. The essential difference between children and adults is that children look for immediate fulfillment of desires and quick satisfaction, while adults try to look at the bigger picture due to the necessity of maintaining their own and their families' existence. This is where the whole area of ​​entrepreneurship and smart investment opens up.

21.10.2024. we presented the first theatrical performance "Money" to young people at the Center for Education "Vinko Bek" from Zagreb, an educational institution that offers programs for blind and partially sighted people. The performance was attended by 15 students from the Department of Secondary Education from all grades (from 1st to 4th grade of high school) and 11 accompanying teachers and 11 students and users from the Dislocated Unit Zagreb (users from educational groups OOS1 aged 7 to 10, OOS2 aged 11 to 15 and OOS4 aged 16 to 21 and students 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 8th grades of elementary school) and 16 educators and accompanying teachers.

We wanted to introduce primary and secondary school students to the topic of money and inform and educate them in a fun way about the history of money, as well as the importance of managing and spending money. 

We wanted to draw attention to the fact that the attitude towards money affects our daily life, family relationships, relationships with friends and how important it is to be financially literate and have a positive attitude towards acquiring and managing money.

The purpose of realizing the play on the topic of money was to inform children and young people about the importance of financial literacy, and the project was aimed at primary and secondary school students. 

Through the play, we tried to break basic prejudices about money (money corrupts people, money buys happiness and love, money destroys freedom, causes stress...).

The response of students, professors and school principals was exceptional, and that is why we have reason to be satisfied with the implementation and results of this demanding project. Especially because after the premiere, we were contacted by elementary and secondary schools from all over Croatia who wanted us to come to their schools and to perform the play "Money" for their students.

The realization of the theater play was not a goal in itself, but we wanted to enable its continuation in primary and secondary schools, local theaters or other suitable spaces throughout Lijepa Naša. It turned out that the two premieres were the first phase of our effort to encourage financial literacy among children and young people, and that we should continue with the performance of the play in schools, initially in Slavonia, and later in the wider area.

Our goal is for this show to be seen by as many students as possible from all over Croatia, especially from smaller, rural areas where such opportunities often do not exist.
