articles.title: Taking the first step is the greatest courage
articles.description: The editor of Poduzetnika Vladimir Mihajlović writes about the first entrepreneurial steps: Taking the first step is the greatest courage!
articles.excerpt: The editor of Poduzetnika Vladimir Mihajlović writes about the first entrepreneurial steps: Taking the first step is the greatest courage!
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Many claim, "you don't become a great entrepreneur overnight" or "the cards have long been dealt in entrepreneurial waters" or "the redistribution is over".

But is it really so?

Take your first step and see for yourself what is true and what is not!

People differ and are determined by many things: gender, height, eye color, emotions, mentality, experiences, preferences, space and time in which they were born. But they all have one thing in common - that they strive for success.

Many of you want to become entrepreneurs, and the truth is that anyone can become one. Although we are all rushing and rushing somewhere, "getting nowhere", we often don't have time, but in the end we all want peace and security, which is not at all easy to achieve.

If we want to succeed in life, we must always be a little better!

Biti Bolji from others, but Biti Bolji from itself.

Today Biti Bolji than yesterday, tomorrow Biti Bolji than we are today. We can all achieve it, we just have to know how, when, what and where.

Starting your own business, that is, working for yourself and not for others, is a "dream" for many young people, as well as adults, beginners, students, and high school students.

Be your own boss! That sounds very proud.

Of course, it is not at all a simple job and you need to have a clear vision of what you want and how you want to achieve something. Entrepreneurship is, it is true, exciting and mostly profitable. Entrepreneurship is the driver of a country, community, city or society, as well as the source of the often mentioned competitiveness. But entrepreneurship is demanding and risky at the same time.

There are thousands of information about entrepreneurship. Everywhere we turn, everyone is writing or talking about entrepreneurship: daily and specialized newspapers, magazines, TV, books, the Internet. You just need to get on the right path and focus your mind on the right thing. Everything has its own written and unwritten rules, as well as directions to follow. We know that it is necessary to work persistently, to come up with business, to be innovative, to turn to the right markets in and outside of Croatia. It is important that we all accept that this is possible regardless of capital, means and equipment, because here, too, man is at the center of everything.

Each of us can start something of our own, sooner or later.

It is usually thought that the problem of starting a business is the money we don't have or we don't have enough of it, and we forget that the center of everything is the entrepreneur - talented, educated, professional, motivated, inspired by positive emotions.

It will sound unreal, but it is important to encourage all citizens, especially young people, students and pupils, in the development of small and medium enterprises. They are the future entrepreneurs who will start life and create the so often mentioned competitiveness.

The market has a place for everyone!

Become part of a brave team that produces new Croatian products, that offers Croatian services, skills, intelligence, knowledge and innovations!

And remember, there is no shame in failing! You need to have the strength to admit it. If you need to stop at some point, wait for another moment or give up something for a while - that's nothing to be ashamed of. I have met many successful and less successful entrepreneurs. None of them were at their peak performance at all times, that is, everyone had good and bad days both privately and professionally. It is important that you play your film in your head and that you are always thinking about how to solve a problem or someone else's problem.

Don't just stop at the first obstacle and think it can't be done!

Put the fear of failure out of your head and start boldly, but with ideas that have the potential to succeed.

Biti Bolji is what drives and motivates all successful people. And success is not guaranteed or written in the stars. Each of us was once at our beginning and started from some zero of our own.

articles.title: How the richness of the Croatian language contributes to the development of entrepreneurship in Croatia
articles.description: About how the richness of the Croatian language contributes to the development of entrepreneurship in Croatia, write: Ivana Prezzi, Magda Barišić, and Suzana Ković
articles.excerpt: About how the richness of the Croatian language contributes to the development of entrepreneurship in Croatia, write: Ivana Prezzi, Magda Barišić, and Suzana Ković
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.sourceAuthor: Ivana Prezzi, Magda Barišić, Suzana Ković
articles.content:
About how the richness of the Croatian language contributes to the development of entrepreneurship in Croatia, written by: Ivana Prezzi, diploma oec., Magda Barišić, diploma oec. and Suzana Ković, prof. of Croatian language and literature, Commercial and Trade School Split

In vocational schools, the correlation between the general education subject Croatian language and a vocational subject such as Entrepreneurship - can be significant and multiple. These two subjects can be connected in several ways. The subject Croatian language includes the development of communication skills, such as reading, writing, speaking and listening. The aforementioned skills are crucial for successful business and entrepreneurship.

Entrepreneurs need to be able to communicate clearly with different stakeholders, including customers, employees, partners and investors. The Croatian language also provides the basis for the development of presentation skills, which are important for entrepreneurs when presenting ideas, products or services to potential clients, investors or partners. This includes public speaking skills, the ability to adapt to the audience, etc. However, when understanding culture and society, the Croatian language can provide insight into the cultural and social contexts in which the entrepreneur operates. Understanding language and culture can help entrepreneurs better understand the needs, preferences and values ​​of their target markets and adapt their business accordingly.

The wealth of Croatian dialects

Croatian is spoken somewhat differently in different areas. Let's take a look at the wealth of distinctions between the three Croatian dialects: Štokavian, Kajkavian and Chakavian, as well as distinguishing dialectalisms that are characteristic of the area of ​​the entire dialect (Chakavisms, Kajkavisms, Štokavisms).

They form a special group of dialectalisms ethnographic dialectalisms, which name a term (type of food and drink, customs, etc.) characteristic of the area where a certain dialect is spoken, e.g. picigin, bevanda, gnocchi, pashticada... Unlike other dialectalisms, there is no substitute for the group of ethnographic dialectalisms in the standard language.

Linguistic identity, and especially its diversity, makes it essential, invaluable, irreplaceable and a wonderful asset of national identity.

A current example that illustrates the correlation between the Croatian language and entrepreneurship can be market research and the creation of marketing strategies for promoting local food and beverages in Croatia. When an entrepreneur wants to start a business in the food and beverage sector in Croatia, understanding the language and culture plays a key role in the success of his business. The Croatian language enables an entrepreneur to communicate with local suppliers, producers and consumers 'in their dialect', facilitating negotiations, agreements and communication in general. Through the study of the Croatian language, the entrepreneur also gains a deeper understanding of the cultural preferences, habits and values ​​of the local population. For example, understanding regional dialects and local expressions can help an entrepreneur tailor marketing messages and products to reflect the specificities of the target market. Also, knowledge of cultural events, traditions and customs can be useful in creating marketing strategies and events that will attract local audiences.

Let's assume that an entrepreneur plans to open a restaurant in Dalmatia, specializing in traditional Dalmatian cuisine. In order to attract local residents and tourists, it is crucial that its marketing strategy is adapted to the Dalmatian mentality and linguistic peculiarities.

By using regional dialects and local expressions, an entrepreneur could create a sense of connection with the local community and attract the attention of the target market. This customized marketing strategy can contribute to a better recognition and attraction of the restaurant among local residents and tourists.

Motivated by the dedication that Aunt Trešnjica wrote in the Dalmatian cookbook for a wedding to a woman from Split: "Don't get bored, you're hungry and you're smart", we connect the vocational course Entrepreneurship with subjects from the Croatian language related to the culture and traditions of the society in which we live. Let's start with branding.

Branding of Dalmatian specialties through creative use of language elements

One of the key aspects of branding is the design of the logo and packaging, which should reflect the Dalmatian atmosphere and attract the attention of consumers. Here, not only the aesthetic aspect is important, but also the linguistic one. By using Dalmatian expressions or dialects on packaging or in product names, entrepreneurs can further emphasize the authenticity and local identity of their specialties. This creates an emotional connection with consumers, especially if these terms are recognizable to the local community.

Adapting language elements in marketing messages or on the products themselves – is also key. Using local expressions in marketing campaigns or on social networks can contribute to creating a sense of belonging and community among consumers.

For example, instead of a standard slogan like Enjoy the flavors of Dalmatia, an entrepreneur could use authentic Dalmatian expressions like Savor moments of the taste of Dalmatia, emphasizing the authenticity and local character of the product. When it comes to the names of products or dishes, entrepreneurs can use local legends, customs or geographical elements. For example, the name The witch's spell for a special type of cake, it can attract attention and encourage consumers to try it. In marketing materials for the Hvar brigade or Polish steamer language elements that emphasize authenticity can also be used, such as Hvor's sea magic or Poljica flavors seasoned with tradition, which additionally emphasizes regional peculiarities.

Cooperation with local influencers or event organizations that include cultural aspects of the Dalmatian region can also be enriched with linguistic elements. Through these activities, entrepreneurs can use language as a means of connecting with consumers while promoting their products. Engaging local influencers who use Dalmatian dialects in their posts can further strengthen brand authenticity. 

Branding of autochthonous Dalmatian specialties

Through all these examples, we see how linguistic elements can be integrated into the branding process of autochthonous Dalmatian specialties in order to further emphasize their authenticity and attract the attention of consumers. In addition to strengthening local identity, these linguistic elements also contribute to spreading awareness of the richness of the Dalmatian culinary tradition, thus contributing to the development of entrepreneurship in Croatia.

How to use websites, social media and online campaigns to spread awareness of Dalmatian specialties also plays a key role in promotion. The integration of language elements into these online platforms allows entrepreneurs to reach a wider audience and connect with consumers on a global scale. Through websites, social media and online campaigns, entrepreneurs can present their products using language that reflects the Dalmatian spirit, thereby creating a connection with consumers and encouraging them to explore the region's rich gastronomic heritage.

In addition to promoting their products, websites, social networks and online campaigns provide a platform to share stories about tradition, history and local customs related to Dalmatian specialties. This form of digital marketing allows entrepreneurs to convey to their consumers a sense of community and pride in a rich cultural heritage, thereby further strengthening brand perception.

Creative use of language is key to success

With all of the above, it is important to point out that the creative use of language is crucial, not only in packaging design and product promotion, but also in all aspects of marketing strategies. Through carefully selected linguistic elements, entrepreneurs can create a unique story about their products, which will simultaneously reflect the Dalmatian spirit and attract the attention of consumers. In addition, integrating linguistic elements into marketing activities allows entrepreneurs to connect with the local community in a deeper way, fostering a sense of belonging and community among consumers. Through these marketing strategies, brands become more than just products – they become a symbol of community and pride in local culture and tradition.

articles.description: The play NOVAC, which promotes financial literacy among children and young people, delighted the audience of all generations at its premiere in Osijek.
articles.excerpt: The play NOVAC, which promotes financial literacy among children and young people, delighted the audience of all generations at its premiere in Osijek.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Organized by the Osijek Association "Biti Bolji" from Osijek, and in cooperation with Fort Forno Theater from Bala, on Friday, April 19, 2024, in Branko Mihaljević's Children's Theater in Osijek, the play premiered Money, as part of a larger artistic and educational project aimed at raising awareness of the importance of financial literacy among children and young people.

The provocative, witty and above all educational text, written by director Robert Raponja and actor Gabrijel Perić, communicated extremely successfully with audiences of all generations. Thanks to the young actors, who convincingly convey the message of the play to the audience, the production team can safely proceed with the planned performances of the play in schools throughout Croatia.

Art provides answers to questions that we cannot get from books and is a part of every person's life.

Namely, the center of the scene is the cute brother Gabi and his younger sister Moni, whose parents are on a trip to Italy, and who, while waiting for the "guardian aunt", still have a little time to take us and themselves into their world of play and imagination.

After only a few sentences, the audience realizes that they are looking at 15-year-old Gabi, a smart, diligent, responsible and serious boy who is extremely fond of learning and knowledge, and his bright but playful sister, 12-year-old Moni, who would rather spend all her time playing. In order to avoid solving the math homework, Moni skillfully and quickly persuades Gabi to play his favorite game "Time Travelers", through which, with extremely interesting language and acting bravado, the brother and sister, now as Siri and Ori, remind us of everything that is worth in life, of all those values ​​that we can and cannot pay for with money, but also of the real value of money throughout the centuries, from antiquity through the Renaissance to the present day.

Through the game of lovable time travelers, whose theme is MONEY, Siri and Ori give us historical insight into the creation and change of money over time. By changing the miniatures of the epochal moments of our past, in a humorous and educational way, they reveal to us the ways in which financial literacy can be raised among young people.

To all those who may still be wondering which is the most important currency in life; how much money is really worth; how much money is enough, too much or too little; will money look like this in the future i can we buy everything with money?, we recommend watching the play Money, which directly and indirectly hides numerous answers.

On Friday 19 April, two premieres of the play Novac were held in Osijek. The Zagreb actors Nina Vidan & Filip Sever performed the play in the first act, and the Osijek actors Monika Duvnjak & Gabrijel Perić played in the second act.

Thank you to everyone who has so far recognized the importance of this educational and artistic project, especially the "Croatia for Children" Foundation for its recognition and financial support through grants.

articles.title: Poduzetnik – who is it?
articles.description: The words entrepreneur and entrepreneurship should not be associated only as synonyms for business operations, they also exist in other spheres of life.
articles.excerpt: The words entrepreneur and entrepreneurship should not be associated only as synonyms for business operations, they also exist in other spheres of life.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Poduzetnik – a word with a thousand meanings, interpretation and analysis. But the most important is in connection with one characteristic that is crucial in any business, profession or sport. It is a trait that trumps all others, regardless of the magnificence of traits such as talent, intelligence, social interaction, honesty, courage. Written by: Darko Balaš, M.Sc. oec., professor and poet from Čepin near Osijek

I would say that this trait embodies all the others, and so rarely do we apply it in our private and business lives. This quality is called persistence.

Like water that finds its way, even when the path is bounded by rocks that are millions of years old, persistence does not see problems as obstacles, but as teachers to study, surround, overcome and eventually learn how to adapt and ultimately survive.

Unfortunately, it is not uncommon here entrepreneur it is associated with quick enrichment, fraud and has a negative connotation among the general public.

I often hear the sentence: "They are all the same!"

But, as always, due to a few dishonest ones, those who achieved goals that seemed almost impossible with their vision, work and persistence also get a bad reputation. All the world's largest economies rest on small businesses, they feed on visions and the realization of those visions through faith, work and perseverance. Especially when that persistence becomes entangled in an almost inextricable web of bureaucracy, bad laws, and local sheriffs who are always looking for their share.

The Republic of Croatia is trying to break up that long-standing network and enable entrepreneurs to take the easiest and most important step: the very beginning. Good initiatives are always born there that will help young startups in their first step, which is usually crucial. Let's not forget: every journey begins with the first step and it is always the hardest. What does that path lead to? Persistence, persistence, persistence.

Being enterprising can easily be translated into a synonym for the Poduzetnik magazine's action: Be better! Be better, be more persistent, be more enterprising! Bring the knowledge of entrepreneurship to schools where future entrepreneurs are born.

We must not associate the words entrepreneur and entrepreneurship only as synonyms for business operations.

Can a person be entrepreneurial in the family, at school, at work, in local self-government, government, united nations?

Were Nikola Tesla or Leonardo da Vinci just ordinary people or entrepreneurs who were looking for sources of funds to realize their unique visions in order to materialize them in reality?

Taking action, moving out of the comfort zone, taking responsibility and embarking on a journey from three fragile ships in order to find a new way to India, which brought Columbus and his crew to America, is inseparably reminiscent of Mata Rimac, who found the way to the fastest electric car of today right here in Croatia.

What do they have in common?

They didn't wait, they took steps to realize their vision.

It's not easy, it's not easy to even come of age and persistently and persistently publish a magazine in print, regardless of the fact that IT technology meant death for all other print editions of Croatian business magazines.

To be persistent, to go further, is a characteristic of this magazine, its editorial staff, all of us columnists and all other wise minds who cooperate with us. One more step further. Another text. Another action. Persistent, brave and enterprising!

articles.excerpt: Time is money, and "Money" is a new play for children and young people organized by the Association Biti Bolji. The media partner is the magazine Poduzetnik.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
The first working agreement was held and acting rehearsals of the fantastic team working on the production and realization of the play "Money" began. The countdown has begun until the premiere in Osijek, which will take place on April 19, 2024, which we are extremely pleased about.

That day has come. We started the realization of the theater play "Money", which looks at the concept of money as an indicator of value from different historical, cultural and geopolitical angles, and through concrete examples explains basic concepts related to money and the monetary system to children and young people. The project holder is Association Biti Bolji from Osijek, and the preparation of the realization and realization of the theatrical performance will be done by the members Fort Forno Theater Association from Bal. The media sponsor of the project is magazine Poduzetnik.

Art provides answers to questions that we cannot get from books and is a part of every person's life.

The basic setting of the theater play

Through fast, interactive and dynamic play, complete with choreography and stage movement, along with music and songs, the actors introduce children to the world of money. Through graphic examples, the actors will vividly portray the history of money and will also explain basic concepts related to money to children through examples. The actors will analyze them in an interactive dialogue with the children.

Siri and Ori are inseparable brother and sister who love to express themselves poetically and musically. Their games and puzzles awaken the dormant imagination and draw everyone present into their imaginative world. Siri is more dominant than her brother, who always starts a lot, but rarely finishes. However, Siri does not feel the most comfortable around strangers, including children, and she also cannot stand the sharp criticism of her brother Ori, who successfully finds flaws in each of Siri's songs and melodies.

In order to travel through the timelines, Siri and Ori need money, which they convert into their currency - time. In this dimension, time invested in work turns into money. Children know best how to fill their time as efficiently as possible, and they come to learn, but how do you get money with that? Siri has enough money to return to their timeline and finally their home, but her brother doesn't because he spent too much on time travel. Their search for the ability to properly manage money takes them on a musical journey of creating a song that unites their acquired experiences.

Space-time brings Ori onto the scene, who has visible traces of time travel to different places. Very confused, he tries to figure out where he is by noticing the crowd and analyzing what he is wearing and the objects around him. Not long after, Siri appears and starts questioning Ori about where he's been and why he decided to act in such an insane way because his antics have caused him to lose all the time credit that allows him to return home.

Target group

The target group is elementary school students (aged 6-15), from the first to eighth grade, and by agreement also students of the first and second grades of secondary schools (aged 15-16).

Time and place for the premiere

The play will be premiered twice at Branko Mihaljević's Children's Theater in Osijek, on April 19, 2024, and we will send an invitation to come to the play to students from Osijek, Osijek-Baranja County, but also to all other interested students from other counties in Slavonia.

After the premiere, it is planned that the play "Money" will be played in primary and secondary schools throughout Croatia, as well as in local theaters, libraries and other suitable venues during the next three years.

Association "Biti Bolji" from Osijek, in May 2023, submitted the project of the theater play "Money" to the Public call for applications of legal entities for (co)financing of programs and projects implemented by the "Croatia for Children" Foundation. We decided to bring this area closer to children through a theater play about money, through art. It has been shown that children remember what they see and hear very well, and the theater performance is a fantastic tool for information and education. Art provides answers to questions that we cannot get from books and is a part of every person's life.

Thank you to the "Croatia for Children" Foundation for recognizing this project and for the financial support through grants, because without their support we would have had a hard time starting the implementation of the project.

articles.title: We want to change the paradigm of global waste disposal
articles.description: This student waste disposal project is the result of the work of three perfectly synergistic people: Rina Crnjaković, Fran Čutura and Nika Bucala.
articles.excerpt: This student waste disposal project is the result of the work of three perfectly synergistic people: Rina Crnjaković, Fran Čutura and Nika Bucala.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
This winning student waste disposal project is the result of great joint work and enthusiasm of three perfectly synergistic people: Rina Crnjaković, Fran Čutura and Nika Bucala.

Presentation of the waste disposal project

Niko Bucalo introduced himself, his team and the project with the words: "Since I was young, I have been interested in the effectiveness and optimization of processes. Not in the sense that I am lazy and don't like work, on the contrary, I enjoy muscular and neurogenesis during physical work, only I don't define work as force multiplied by distance traveled, but rather as force multiplied by air distance. I have always considered this passion for finding shortcuts as a life calling and wanted to turn it into work. principles of optimization, I was brought up with great respect for mother nature, I love sustainability.

The ReCLo project is based on the template for optimizing the textile supply chain through the use of the 'Internet of Textiles' platform. Our goal is to connect different stakeholders in the textile industry, from manufacturers and suppliers, through distributors, to retailers, in order to create a more efficient system of textile reuse and recycling. Figuratively, we want to turn the textile industry into a confectionery industry, where we know that the remains of one cake can be used for some other cake. The product is in the proof-of-concept phase, and will be out by the end of the year."

How and when was the idea to start this project born?

The idea for the ReCLo project came after a year and a half of physical work in the sector according to the protocol: collect waste - categorize - process - and put it back on the market. After looking at the statistics of the sector a year ago, we came to a startling calculation that on average 20% of input material is not used by production, which led us to think about how we can get to that problem - the problem of company losses when dealing with such waste, but also losses for our environment.

We realized that there is a big discrepancy between prescribed care methods and care performance, a gap between theory and practice. In translation, there is a huge lack of communication among the waste disposal stakeholders, while there are many digital solutions for textile waste disposal, they are not interoperable, networked, and do not have a common denominator. This is how our platform was created, which is often nicknamed the "Internet of Textiles". We have already won over several juries with our idea, including this one from HAMAG. As a team, we share a vision of creating a sustainable solution to the problem of textile waste.

You are the founder of the Alavera Design Association, what is it about?

Yes, it all started as an idea that we would be one student upcycling a studio on the fashion scene of the city of Zagreb that other textile companies will use for their socially responsible part of business, to which they will donate waste and which will produce new things from it, which is what we have been doing for the past two years. Establishment fashion studio Alavera was the seed of this software solution; digitization of production and enabling the green transition of business that we are working on today. After launching a fashion brand, we realized how much the sector needed a digital solution to improve the efficiency and sustainability of textile processes.

What motivates and moves you?

What motivates us is faith in change and the desire to create a positive impact on the world around us. Innovation has always been the driving force that enables solving problems in new and creative ways and drives progress. The project will bring a protocol for the development of sustainable solutions for the textile industry and will serve to raise awareness of the importance of sustainability among consumers.

Also, it motivates us to see a stimulating environment that allows young people to express their ideas and test them in project initiatives. For all that, once again, thank you to HAMAG BICRO for the opportunity!

After that, the plan is to play the play "Money", after the premiere, in primary and secondary schools, local theaters, libraries and other suitable venues for the next three years.

The goal is to raise awareness of money and financial literacy among children and young people and to destroy prejudices and myths about this topic.

Prejudices and myths about money

Today it is unthinkable to live without money. Money is the topic of almost all our conversations, whether we complain that we don't have enough, or that everything is too expensive. Money is associated with myths that we still believe today, and it is these myths about money that limit us from truly enjoying your financial freedom.

It is important to talk about money because as long as it is a taboo subject, nothing will change. Therefore, let's start dispelling the myths associated with money and make the young generation aware that it is money is a resource that will enable them to achieve their goals, their desires, to live the life they want to live.

articles.title: The project "Biti Bolji" goes further: member of the PBZ Management Board, Vedrana Jelušić Kašić, will speak to the students about financial literacy.
articles.description: The "Biti Bolji" project goes further: PBZ Board member Vedrana Jelušić Kašić will speak to students about financial literacy.
articles.excerpt: The "Biti Bolji" project goes further: PBZ Board member Vedrana Jelušić Kašić will speak to students about financial literacy.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
As part of the eponymous project of the Osijek Association "Biti Bolji", which has been bringing motivational speakers, mainly entrepreneurs, to Croatian schools for 10 years, who convey their experiences to young people and inspire them to realize their visions and dreams, so far 200 lecturers have given more than 250 lectures, which have been listened to by more than 42,000 students.

Thus, on Tuesday, September 19, 2023, on the same day, Hospitality and Tourism School Osijek and Braća Radić School of Economics in Đakovo to visit a member of the PBZ Management Board Vedrana Jelušić Kašić.

In addition to introducing the students to her career path, Vedrana Jelušić Kašić will also hold a lecture with the intriguing title "Life without money". After the lecture, he will discuss with the students the importance of financial literacy and how to acquire the necessary financial competencies of the future.

Vedrana Jelušić Kašić - short BIO

Vedrana Jelušić Kašićshe is a member of the Management Board of PBZ, in charge of the Area of Business with Medium and Large Enterprises and Investment Banking. She is the president of the Supervisory Board of PBZ-Leasing d.o.o.

Before assuming her position at PBZ, she was a partner in the Financial Consulting Department and led and coordinated initiatives with private clients, M&A activities and corporate management at the level of the Adriatic region.

He has more than 20 years of managerial experience gained in international financial institutions. Before joining Deloitte, she was the director of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) for Croatia, Slovenia, Hungary and Slovakia, responsible for the strategy and execution of the business plan through investments and support for institutional reforms in those countries. In the role of Senior Banker of the EBRD responsible for the financing of the Agribusiness sector, Vedrana directly managed more than 40 transactions in 12 countries of Central and Southeastern Europe.

She was a member of supervisory boards in several food and trade companies in the region, including Atlantic Grupa, Tikveš, VF Komerc and others. She gained additional business experience at Raiffeisen Bank in Croatia, Merrill Lynch Private Client Group in the USA, Croatian National Bank and Monte Titoli in Italy.

She holds a master's degree in the field of international economics and finance at Brandeis University, Massachusetts, USA, and graduated from the Faculty of Economics in Zagreb. She attended courses in the field of finance at the Wirtschaftsuniversität and the Institut für Wirtschaftwissenschaften in Vienna. He holds the Financial Times Diploma of the United Kingdom for non-executive directors, members of supervisory boards.

Here is what Vedrana Jelušić Kašić says about the importance of the need for financial literacy

Financial literacy enables better planning of current expenses and future investments, which we expect will enrich our business or private life. Financial literacy, as a combination of knowledge and skills, also contributes to our personal greater resilience, especially during certain unpredictable life events and situations. The way we decide to earn, spend, save and invest wisely can contribute to the well-being of not only the individual, but also society, as well as the stability of the entire economy.

articles.title: Theater performance "Money"
articles.description: After ten years of working with young people, we decided to start the realization of the theater play "Money". Today there are different forms of education...
articles.excerpt: After ten years of working with young people, we decided to start the realization of the theater play "Money". Today there are different forms of education...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Ten years ago Association "Biti Bolji" launched the basic project "Biti Bolji-Be Better" in which she involved young people from 30 high schools, 12 primary schools and 5 faculties in Croatia, more than 200 workshops, lectures, forums, discussions, theater performances were held, and more than 41,000 young people from Croatia listened to and actively participated in the project. Numerous lecturers and guests, about 160 of them, from entrepreneurs to public figures, visited schools and colleges and shared their experiences with pupils and students. Through a series of activities that we carried out in Croatia, we wanted to encourage pupils and students to acquire all the necessary competencies needed for life and work.

After ten years of working with young people, we decided to start the realization of the theater play "Money". Today, there are various forms of financial competence education. Workshops, lectures, applications, lectures in schools and other educational institutions, financial institution courses, books, manuals... All of these are tools for better familiarization with financial competencies.

This time we decided on a theater show about money in order to bring this area closer to children through art. It has been shown that children remember what they see and hear very well, and the theater performance is a fantastic tool for information and education. Art provides answers to questions that we cannot get from books and is a part of every person's life.

Why a theater performance?

Financial literacy is the possession of certain knowledge, skills and attitudes that, along with quality information, contribute to making appropriate decisions related to finances. This is the knowledge that is needed to function in today's environment. Financial ignorance can have long-term consequences for each individual, on their social status, which especially applies to children and young people. More than ever, children need knowledge and competences that will enable them to be included in life faster and easier and to choose a future profession.

The results of financial literacy research conducted by HANFA (Croatian Financial Services Supervision Agency) for several years show that young people (children) are a particularly vulnerable group. That is why it is important to make young people, especially children, aware of active and responsible management of personal finances.

Target group and premiere of the play

The target group is primary school students (ages 6-15), from the first to eighth grades, and students in the first and second grades of high schools (ages 15-16), of both sexes. We plan to premiere the play twice in Branko Mihaljević's Children's Theater Osijek or a similar adequate space by the end of April 2024 at the latest, and to which we will invite students from all Slavonian counties. The realization of the theater play is not the only goal, but the goal is to continue its presentation even after the premiere in primary and secondary schools throughout Croatia for the next three years.

We want to realize the theater performance in the period from November 1, 2023 to May 31, 2024. We will succeed in the implementation only with the cooperation and support of professors and principals of schools, the local community, companies, entrepreneurs, citizens, and finally the students we want to educate.

articles.title: Every obstacle can be an opportunity to create a new project
articles.description: Every obstacle can be an opportunity to create a new project, says Stipo Margić, a second-year student at the University of Split.
articles.excerpt: Every obstacle can be an opportunity to create a new project, says Stipo Margić, a second-year student at the University of Split.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Stipo Margić – second-year student of the specialist graduate study in Computer Science at the University Department of Professional Studies in Split.

Stipo does not like to burden his loved ones, friends and colleagues with everyday obstacles, but always tries to find a solution. His motto is that there is no problem that a living man cannot solve.

Stipo Margić, in addition to studying, is the founder and president of the Liberato Association, which was originally created as a solution to the situation he found himself in four years ago. Today, the Association deals with the development of projects that will make life easier for young people, students, people with disabilities and people with limited mobility in the long term. Stipo has won a number of awards, the most recent of which was the award for DisCloud at the 20th International Innovation Exhibition ARCA.

Stipo has achieved a large number of educational, sectoral and intersectoral collaborations with the Association, of which he is extremely proud. He is fond of computing and IT technology, so everything he does is a kind of entertainment. He looks forward to developing new projects and creating new innovations for the market. Every new obstacle is a new challenge for Stipe. He does not spend his time looking for excuses and "whining", but tirelessly searches for a way to reach the goal.

Why computer science? They say that you are a special person, innovative, versatile, an excellent example social entrepreneur. What does being a social entrepreneur mean to you?

The reason is simple. Ever since high school education, I have had a strong love for programming and related computer skills. Also, due to my health situation, this type of occupation provides me with prerequisites for further development on a business and private level. For me, being a social entrepreneur means investing all my resources – knowledge, skills, time and resources – in order to solve social problems that other participants in society don't see, don't want to see or don't have the resources to fix. I started this entrepreneurial venture with my heart. What motivated me the most was the realization that I could use my knowledge and programming skills to help people with disabilities and encourage them to be more involved in society.

You are the president of the association Liberato, which was founded by students of the University Department of Professional Studies in Split. When and how did this story begin?

It all started with the creation of an idea that would solve the problem of finding a place where I could celebrate my birthday. Namely, when planning my birthday celebration, I couldn't find information anywhere about the degree of accessibility of entrances to catering establishments, so out of anger, in an affect, I told my friends that I would create a map myself that would provide this information, which is extremely important to people with disabilities, parents with children in strollers and people with limited mobility. The history, present and future of the Liberato association starts from that moment. The association advocates for increasing the rate of inclusion of young people with disabilities in society and improving their quality of life.

With the support of the University Department of Professional Studies i of the student entrepreneurial incubator SPIK@ you have developed a number of projects...

All the projects we have developed are extremely dear to me, and I would like to single out the LiberatoTalk project in particular. It is a project created by students with our teachers and mentors Ivona Jukić and Antonija Roje, with whom we developed the most cooperation at the University Department of Professional Studies in Split. The project is designed to give young people the opportunity to acquire new skills and knowledge in the business world and to reduce the gap between students and students with disabilities to enable them to enter the labor market more easily.

To what extent does our system encourage and enable certain adaptations for students with disabilities?

The system provides students with disabilities reasonable ways and types of adjustments within the higher education itself, such as a longer time for writing the exam, an adapted font of professional literature and the possibility of taking the exam orally instead of in writing. Also, I believe that people need to change their view of the world. People with disabilities have a wrong view of the education system, and I would recommend that they definitely give higher education a chance. Furthermore, students often do not look favorably because they feel that it is being made too easy for them, not knowing what problems they face on a daily basis. In the end, professors and professional associates have a certain amount of fear about how to approach people with disabilities, how to treat them and to what extent they need adaptation.

articles.title: How the study completely changed the perception of entrepreneurship for one student
articles.description: I emphasize the fact that the study has completely changed my perception of entrepreneurship as one of the more important implications of studying.
articles.excerpt: I emphasize the fact that the study has completely changed my perception of entrepreneurship as one of the more important implications of studying.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Laura Lara Gizdić is currently participating in the PlanStart project in collaboration with HGK-ŽK Split, where under the mentorship of teacher Ivona Jukić, her colleague Ana Bilić and Laura Lara are creating a business plan for a micro-entrepreneur who owns a foreign language school.

Laura is a member Student entrepreneurial incubator and she is engaged in the Office for Business Cooperation, and she spends her free time hanging out with family and friends, going for walks and trips by the sea, and regularly watching sports events. She is mostly focused on student obligations and entrepreneurial projects in which she participates together with her fellow students. She is an analytical and disciplined person who never gives up, and she believes that this persistence is the key to developing an entrepreneurial spirit.

What attracts you to the world of entrepreneurship?

The experience of studying at the undergraduate studies was really excellent, I learned so much in theory and practice, I met so many promising opportunities, listened to inspiring guest lectures, participated in various projects and, most importantly, incredibly expanded my horizons in all areas of personal and professional development. All this only motivated me further to continue studying at a specialist study, where there is a really wide spectrum of opportunities for all students who have the will, desire and urge to do something more. One step in this can be inclusion in the Student Entrepreneurship Incubator. This is exactly how students can develop and exchange ideas, meet colleagues and participate in workshops and conferences in the field of entrepreneurship, together with our professors who are approachable and willing to help. Among other things, this is what attracted me to the world of entrepreneurship, inspired me to step out of my comfort zone and proactively think about entrepreneurship.

I emphasize the fact that the study has completely changed my perception of entrepreneurship as one of the more important implications of studying.

You have been involved in a number of projects...

I am happy that I had the opportunity to be involved in a number of projects during my studies, and I believe that in each of them I managed to anticipate very important life and business lessons, valuable advice and various educational experiences. The project in which I participated twice and which particularly impressed me, is related to the education of students at startup workshops. Their ideas, creativity, confidence and teamwork absolutely left me speechless. I believe that stereotypes about the generations to come will be eliminated by some of these young people. The innovativeness and interest they showed, attentive listening and critical thinking, and openness to cooperation, give a hint that their entrepreneurial spirit can potentially be the basis for the arrival of a new generation of successful entrepreneurs.

You say that raising awareness of society and community and helping others has become imperative, is it?

Social entrepreneurship is the type of entrepreneurship that I have always had the greatest affinity for and which I would like to continue exploring. I believe that in our country there is capacity to implement at least some segments of social entrepreneurship in the operations of every company. Making society and the community aware of current problems has become necessary because it can be a significant step in creating a more humane and tolerant society.

My definition of success varies depending on the topic, but in the context of entrepreneurship, the word try is a synonym for the word success. I consider success to be the courage of a person to venture into entrepreneurship, to do everything in his power to make the venture succeed, to put in the maximum effort and act responsibly throughout the process, regardless of the outcome.

I am focused on finishing my graduate studies and at the same time I am gaining experience thanks to student projects and working. If I decide to start my own entrepreneurial venture, I know that I will have wonderful people by my side who will support me in this.

articles.title: To be a good entrepreneur, you need to be transparent and honest
articles.description: In entrepreneurship, you must be transparent and honest, because these are two important determinants that help you realize your own business.
articles.excerpt: In entrepreneurship, you must be transparent and honest, because these are two important determinants that help you realize your own business.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Tea Petra Debak - is a third-year student of the trade and tourism management undergraduate professional study at the University Department of Professional Studies in Split, who claims: "To be good at entrepreneurship, you have to be transparent and honest. These are two important determinants that help you realize your own business."

Tea Petra is an artist and entrepreneur, her own boss, for whom the path to entrepreneurship in music was opened by her studies. She has never lacked the desire for progress and believes that in entrepreneurship it hides an opportunity for the expansion of that desire she has for music, i.e. the violin. The urge to go into entrepreneurship was present from a young age, although no one in the family followed that path. Taught to work and discipline, education at a music school and economic science brought her a lot of good things on which she can start building her talent, as well as her life's vocation.

They say that you are eloquent, hardworking and creative. How important are these qualities for the development and success of every person in life and work?

Study he largely showed me the way to entrepreneurship. During my studies, I came into contact with wonderful professors and young colleagues who, in addition to regular learning and knowledge, supported me in what I passionately wanted, which is to learn to be my own boss and my own person. My qualities fit perfectly into the environment in which I study. I learned that transparency and honesty are essential for the development of a good entrepreneur.

Along with your studies, you play the violin professionally. How important is art, in your case music, for the development of a person?

I believe that music is universal and that everyone can understand it because it speaks in a simple language. For example, everyone understands the pleasure that music creates while listening to a favorite song. That's how I took my studies seriously, but with a dose of pleasure. Likewise, I encountered discipline at the music school. It was necessary to practice for months in order for the composition to "come out". I transferred that to my studies. Colloquiums and exams must not suffer. This discipline is transferred to life. You do what you love, that's the key.

What is the right moment to enter the business? An entrepreneurial story doesn't necessarily have to be a success, but persistence and hard work will never go unnoticed.

From a young age, I went to various performances, attended extracurricular activities, constantly worked with my hands, manually, but also read. When I enrolled in management studies, I joined the Student Entrepreneurship Incubator. The professor, who is also the head of the Incubator, guided me into entrepreneurship because I already had a vision that I expressed to her. That's how I got the opportunity to participate in workshops where I gave motivational presentations about my entry into entrepreneurship. I am currently doing an internship at the Office for Business Cooperation. In particular, I had the opportunity to participate in a competition as part of a team to solve a certain marketing problem for one of the leading Croatian retail chains, where we also won an award, and the last opportunity I got was to participate in the Women and Money conference in Split. All the mentioned opportunities still create the right moment in which I will seriously venture into the creative - entrepreneurial waters.

Platon himself said that music in the country is crucial for the progress of the economy. My desire is to be an inspiration to young people with what is my vocation, which is to work and live from what you love. I believe that the education I received and my talent for music can result in a very nice entrepreneurial story in the future.

As part of the "Leadership Academy for Civil Society Organizations" project, a pilot program was implemented to develop the leadership potential of elementary school children. The implementation of the pilot program was led by the Association Good afternoon, with many years of experience in implementing programs for children and youth with the aim of developing civil society, and the 5th and 6th grade students of Pavlek Miškine Primary School from Zagreb participated.

Through previous individual and mentoring work, the students developed their leadership competencies by detecting 4 pressing problems in their local community, for which they immediately offered creative solutions and requested additional support. articles.title: Biti Bolji – Be Better: We continue with the mission of educating young people about entrepreneurship
articles.description: In these challenging times, in a world that is changing at an incredible speed, young people need to be encouraged to persevere in realizing their dreams...
articles.excerpt: In these challenging times, in a world that is changing at an incredible speed, young people need to be encouraged to persevere in realizing their dreams...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Every new knowledge is of inestimable value to young people and can bring great changes in their lives. That is precisely why, with the mission of educating young people about entrepreneurship, Association Biti Bolji and a magazine Poduzetnik continue to bring successful entrepreneurs to Slavonian secondary schools.

“Being an entrepreneur/manager” – conversation in Đakovo and Donji Miholjec

dr. med. Biljana Ignatovska, radiology specialist, owner and director Polyclinic Arcadia from Daruvar she visited December 9, 2022. Braća Radić School of Economics in Đakovo i Secondary school Donji Miholjac where she talked to about 80 students.

Biljana told the students how, due to a combination of life circumstances, she started thinking about entering the world of entrepreneurship, and she took over the leadership of the Polyclinic in 2019. She talked about the family business and expressed her satisfaction that she has the opportunity to work with her father and emphasized that she will be happy if her daughter decides to work with her one day. She told the students to follow their ideas, educate themselves and find their passion in it, and in the end she added: "Don't give up on your dreams, make mistakes and regardless of the mistakes you make, move on bravely!"

"Being a manager/entrepreneur" - a conversation at a high school in Našić

December 20, 2022 inIsidor Kršnjavo Secondary School in Našice Frano Šušnjara from Dubai and Goran Suša from Zagreb gave lectures to students who wanted to listen to these interesting guests. Thus, a total of 340 students of this school listened to their lecture.

Frano Šušnjara he is a political scientist by profession, and has been on the business path since he was 26 years old as a very successful manager. He spent most of his career in the automotive industry and worked at the very top of Renault in Paris. Few people manage to break into the very top management of large companies, and Frano succeeded in this, and we are grateful to him for agreeing to tell the students about his life's journey. Today, Frano is the Group Managing Director at Stellantis for the Middle East  – Dubai, United Arab Emirates. But he wishes to return to Croatia, because as he says - Croatia is a brand.

"Each country, each city has its own challenges, adaptation needs and difficulties in the same. Different cultures, legal frameworks, customs and languages are a feature of every society, so adaptation also requires a certain amount of effort and persistence. I think that this need for a 'reset' and permanent learning with great persistence is something that has become part of everyday habit. Branding Croatia is not just a jersey, prosciutto or a UNESCO plaque on a monument. It is something much deeper, more precise, something that requires time, professional work and effort in order to clearly define the value and uniqueness that we can offer behind the term 'Croatia'."

Goran Suša He was born in Vinkovci, where he graduated from high school of economics, after which he went to Zagreb and graduated in Economics, majoring in Organization and Management. From the first working day, he focuses on HR, with specialization in Organization, salary and reward systems.

"In 2011, I moved to France to the headquarters of the Lactalis Group, where for the next 6 years I held the positions of International Mobility Manager and Compensation Manager for the Group. In 2017, I moved to Lille, where I assumed the position of Compensation & Benefit Leader for the Kiabi Group, and we will remain there until I return to Croatia, in the summer of 2020, where I assume the position of Director of Strategic Human Resources Planning for HT. In 2022, I open my own consulting firm for advising strategic of human resources management with specialization in salary, reward and benefit policies and systems and their strategic alignment with the vision, mission and strategy of both the HR department and the entire company."

These versatile "boys" particularly impressed the students with their successes, with a final message: "Be authentic and let what you do be in harmony with your heart and head, follow your heart and include reason in it. We are all creators of our own collage and our own experiences, and you be the ones who will start the Croatian economy and present our country in an even better light."

We are happy that the Poduzetnik magazine, thanks to the donation of various companies, reaches the addresses of about 300 schools, and we hope that with its positive and inspiring content, it will encourage the spread of an entrepreneurial mindset among young people, who are our future and from whom everything starts. Since we are all invited to spread the meaning and importance of entrepreneurship among young people in Croatia, we invite you to join the campaign "Every student an entrepreneur" and to donate to one, five or more schools with an annual subscription to the magazine Poduzetnik.

articles.description: Yesterday at the Faculty of Agrobiotechnological Sciences in Osijek, a meeting for young people "10 years of Biti Bolji!" was held, organized by the Osijek association...
articles.excerpt: Yesterday at the Faculty of Agrobiotechnological Sciences in Osijek, a meeting for young people "10 years of Biti Bolji!" was held, organized by the Osijek association...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Association "Biti Bolji", founded and led by the good spirit of entrepreneurship Vladimir Mihajlović, ten years ago launched the eponymous project "Biti Bolji" with the aim of educating and involving young people in entrepreneurial topics before they enter the labor market. They do this through visits to schools, where, through motivational lectures, pupils and students meet some of the most successful Croatian entrepreneurs, who share their valuable business and life experiences firsthand.

During 10 years, the Association organized the visits of 150 entrepreneurs and realized 200 different programs for about 40 thousand young people.

On the tenth anniversary of the project, in cooperation with the Poduzetnik media platform, the association decided to solemnly celebrate its outstanding results and past work with a conference in Osijek Faculty of Agrobiotechnological Sciences. In the crowded hall of the modern FAZOS, a large audience, including about 200 young people, attentively followed all presentations by entrepreneurs and managers from various industries.

With the aim of encouraging the gathered young people to creativity, work and independence, and to acquire the skills and competences necessary for the future, numerous inspiring speakers told their stories.

After the welcoming speech of the host, the president of the Association Biti Bolji and the editor of the magazine Poduzetnik Vladimir Mihajlović, serial entrepreneur and co-owner of the media platform Poduzetnik Fire Bagatin he gave an inspiring lecture on leadership, emphasizing that in the end, each of us is our own brand and our own leader.

Business mentor Fran Mikuličić, who helped the realization of numerous successful leaders, through a conversation with a proactive graduate from Osijek Lovro Tašić revealed to us what the Biti Bolji really means!

A prominent Istrian entrepreneur spoke about leadership in victory and defeat Plinio Cuccurin, and the general director of Bosch for Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina Mirsada Kudrić she informed young people about the topics of green economy, sustainability and CO2 neutrality, as the top topics of today's era.

Entrepreneur in medicine dr. Biljana Ignatovska, the director of the Arcadia Polyclinic, spoke about her transition from the state sector to entrepreneurial waters, stressing that the fact that she is "her own boss" is, first of all, an invaluable feeling of freedom for her, which she wouldn't trade for anything.

After being the director Robert Raponja i Vladimir Mihajlovic briefly presented their new joint project in the making, the play "Money", which, with the aim of financial literacy for children, would be performed in schools from 2024, Jan Drstvenšek, a graduate of the School of Applied Arts and Design from Osijek, presented his ideas about entrepreneurship through a concept he called "5%". Namely, on the example of his creative entrepreneurial project, he came to the conclusion that nothing comes at first or immediately, and that sometimes even progress with a dynamic of 5% by 5% is quite enough for successful progress on the way to the goal.

After Jan's presentation, the professional musician and chief manager of the Yamaha Music School licensed system for Croatia, BiH and Serbia Olja Dešić he made us aware of interesting facts from the world of music that we rarely think about while enjoying the concerts of our favorite artists, as well as how the entrepreneurial mindset in the music industry thinks.

from Vinkovci Goran Suša, HR consultant in the field of salary and reward systems, spoke about his alternating business journey, his dreams during college, the experience of working in a corporation and working for himself, as well as his experiences from a ten-year career in France.

Member of the Board of Erste Card Club Anita Markota Štriga, in conversation with the moderator Sasa Uranjek, using her own example, she wanted to make young people aware that they can realize everything they dream about now, regardless of the circumstances, but only if they believe in themselves and in their set goal.

Director of the Human Resources Department in the hundred-year-old company KONČAR Damir Sertić he spoke about current trends in employment and the future of the labor market, and as sugar at the end, in a dynamic panel dedicated to communication, with a moderator Fran Mikuličić, they participated Manuel Šola, founder and director of the communications agency Communication laboratory and co-owner of the public relations company Grizli komunikacije Thomas Bauer. Today, communication is EVERYTHING, but public communication is still a professional field, the panelists agreed. In order to learn to communicate successfully, it is necessary to activate several types of intelligence, to network well from an early age, to constantly learn, to be informed, to be educated, to be exposed to quality communication channels and contents, such as this conference in Osijek.

Donor concert by Nena Belan and Olja Dešić

The crown of the whole meeting was the end of the day and the donor concert. In the evening hours, in Branko Mihaljević's children's theater, conference participants enjoyed the concert Nene Belana with Olja Dešić i Josip Radić, where the audience with a lot of emotion, together with the performers, sang all of Belan's hits, and some even danced. 😊

When we started the project 10 years ago "Biti Bolji - Be Better", we had no idea how it would become our brand, but also enable young people to participate in a series of activities in primary and secondary schools and colleges.

The creative energy remained the same as at the beginning of the project, and young people are calling us to visit more and more. We are proud of everything we have achieved in the past 10 years and continue with the same enthusiasm. Generations of students have become grown-up young people of whom we are proud, and we still feel "young" with them. For this reason, we want to mark the 10th anniversary of the launch of the "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project in a special way.

This meeting is the crown of our ten years of work with young people, and will be held on April 27, 2023 (Thursday), starting at 10 a.m., in the premises of the Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek.

At this meeting, young people will have the opportunity to listen to 10 panels, be in the company of famous entrepreneurs, managers, musicians... The topics of the panels will be adapted to the interests and needs of young people, and all visitors can enter for free.

On the same day, in Branko Mihaljević's children's theater in Osijek, a concert will be held starting at 7 p.m Nene Belana i Olje Dešić under the name "THANK YOU!". We will invite pupils, students and guests to the concert. We will give away concert tickets to young people, and donors and sponsors will enable us to realize this.

Basic goals of the project "Biti Bolji - Be Better“

  • Education of pupils and students about entrepreneurship and encouragement of entrepreneurship.
  • Encouraging creativity, leadership, communication, responsibility. persistence in work, self-esteem, independence and ability to solve problems and other skills and competencies necessary for entrepreneurship.
  • Preparation of pupils and students (young people) for continuing education and the labor market.
  • Encouraging pupils and students to start their own business or self-employment.

More than 40,000 pupils and students have so far seen presentations, panels, discussions, theater performances, concerts and workshops as part of the Biti Bolji project, and about 250 guest lecturers (entrepreneurs, managers, athletes, actors, musicians...) visited pupils and students.

articles.title: The inextricable connection between entrepreneurship and education
articles.description: On November 14, 2022, Daniel Ackermann, co-owner of the digital agency Degordian from Zagreb, spoke to about 80 students...
articles.excerpt: On November 14, 2022, Daniel Ackermann, co-owner of the digital agency Degordian from Zagreb, spoke to about 80 students...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Guided by the idea that it is the social responsibility of all of us to spread the meaning and importance of entrepreneurship among young people in Croatia, because only they can contribute to the stronger economic development of our country in the long term, from the very beginning we strive to point out to young people the undeniable fact that there is nothing I cannot accomplish and yes are the creators of their own future.

Every new knowledge for young people is of inestimable value and can bring big changes in their lives, that's why we organized new visits of entrepreneurs to Slavonian schools.

Daniel Ackermann

Daniel Ackermann, co-owner of a digital agency Degordian from Zagreb, November 14, 2022 he talked to about 80 students Electrical Engineering and Traffic School Osijek and Trade and Commercial School "Davor Milas" Osijek.

Daniel has been in business since the age of 15, and he started his first company at the age of 22, in 2009, during the worst recession. He told the students about his beginnings and reasons for entering entrepreneurship, about the ups and downs he experienced along the way, about the successes and awards he won, but also about why his employees are satisfied. He mentioned the fact that his only goal in starting the company at the age of 22 was to employ his friends, so that they could all do what they love together and be happy at the same time.

Daniel told the students to do what they love and be the best at it, adding that money should not be the primary motive for starting a business. He also said that our country offers great opportunities for work, and it is also a beautiful country that successful entrepreneurial stories will make even better, and invited them to stay in Croatia.

Simona Zavratnik

Simona Zavratnik, owner and director of the company Petrokov d.o.o. from Zagreb, November 24, 2022 held a very interesting and motivating lecture for about 100 students at the Osijek Hospitality and Tourism School and the Valpovo High School.

Simona managed to transform a small family business, which started in a garage, into a modern company with 200 employees. By expanding the assortment, she introduced radical changes in the company's way of doing business, which was crucial for success.

The strength of this woman is in her many years of experience in different positions in completely different branches, as well as in teamwork, exceptional persistence, discipline and complete dedication to work. She was born in Maribor, Slovenia, and at the age of 19 she moved to Austria, where she still lives today. "My life basically takes place in the triangle Austria - Slovenia - Croatia", said Simona.

She spoke to the students about the importance of lifelong learning, adding that the diploma is a tool that will help them strengthen their self-confidence. She said that it is important to become aware of what you are good at and improve it, but at the same time remain who you are - authentic. She emphasized the importance of cultivating a sense of gratitude with the message: "Believe in yourself and don't concentrate on what you don't have, but be grateful for what you already have because often these are the 'little things' that we don't notice."

There is no shortage of positive and inspiring entrepreneurial stories in the Poduzetnik magazine, and so far it has been proven that they are an excellent incentive for spreading the entrepreneurial mindset among young people. Therefore, with the mission of educating young people about entrepreneurship, we launched a campaign last year "Every student an entrepreneur" thanks to which the magazine Poduzetnik reached the addresses of 350 primary and secondary schools throughout the year.

These days, we are continuing with the campaign, with the aim of gathering entrepreneurs who will recognize its value and enable the Poduzetnik magazine to continue arriving at the addresses of 500 Croatian primary and secondary schools for the next year. We believe that you will recognize the value of this campaign and support us in our efforts to bring an entrepreneurial mindset to every Croatian school, to every corner of Lijepa Naša... because only by working together can we make this country a better place to live!

Join the campaign and donate an annual subscription to the magazine Poduzetnik to one or more Croatian schools!
