articles.title: Goran Šuša: The world rests on the young!
articles.description: How many times have we heard or said the famous saying ourselves: "The world rests on the young"?! - writes HR consultant Goran Šuša.
articles.excerpt: How many times have we heard or said the famous saying ourselves: "The world rests on the young"?! - writes HR consultant Goran Šuša.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
We need to continue to encourage entrepreneurship even more and thus further improve the competitiveness of the Croatian economy. In the economic sense, only higher productivity of our economy can save us from emigration of young people - writes HR consultant in the field of salary and reward system Goran Šuša (letZ talk C&B).

How many times have we heard or said the famous saying ourselves: "The world rests on the young"?!

To begin with, let's think about what we are leaving them

In Croatia, unfortunately, for many years we have had a trend of strong emigration, especially of young people, where this something, which we all build and create together, should remain.

I am happy that after a long absence from Croatia, with the return of my family to Lijepa Naša, we are improving the bad statistics at least a little, wanting to (re)turn these negative trends with our work, experience and knowledge and show that we can do something good in entrepreneurship, and ultimately succeed.

After returning from abroad, where I gained experience and knowledge, I now look at my own country with different eyes. Every country has its own specificities and problems, and so does Croatia. However, it should be noted that there are many opportunities for progress and development in our country, and there is plenty of unused potential. Unfortunately, these opportunities often do not come to life due to structural problems that persist or are resolved too slowly, which is, among other things, one of the main reasons for the continued trend of emigration from the country.

In order to have good basic principles, we urgently need to start working on school reform, which, unfortunately, after a short-term takeoff, still stoppeda

I am of the opinion that we should focus on practical work, that is, enable high-quality and serious school and student internships that can attract young talents to our area and make an early selection for future potential. Here I welcome the initiatives that the HR community is working with the Legislature.

I can't help but remember my high school days, where several professors, especially professors from Entrepreneurship, already instilled in me a love for economics, numbers and entrepreneurship. I am sure that they helped me draw an entrepreneurial path on my own life map, which finally came true after a little more than 20 years since I left school. Back then, and I have the feeling that it is still the same today, everything was based on the will and enthusiasm of individual professors to pass on part of their knowledge, enthusiasm and enthusiasm to us.

We must not forget the Legislator, who has the task of continuing with the tax reform in order to increase Croatia's attractiveness to young people. Despite all the nice and useful initiatives, without this step we will not reduce the trend of emigration of personnel in which that same country has invested a lot.

Personally, I like the inspiring educational model in which students spend half of their time at work, and the other half in student desks, and at the end, in the final paper, they connect what they have learned from theory with practical application. This type of education and work is an excellent combination, thanks to which many young talents develop, who eventually stay to work in the companies that gave them their first opportunity.

Congratulations to Poduzetnik magazine on its 17th birthday!

I believe that my generation of entrepreneurs has the responsibility and task of passing on their story and advice, either through parenting, formal education, or initiatives and projects such as those carried out by the association "Biti Bolji" and the magazine Poduzetnik, which will surely influence the story of a future entrepreneur. I had the opportunity to speak to Slavonian students about my entrepreneurial journey. If after each lecture only one student decided to stay in Croatia and start entrepreneurship, we have already done a lot!

I heartily congratulate the 17th birthday of the magazine Poduzetnik and the 10th birthday of the project "Biti Bolji"! I am happy that in this very place I can read the stories of young entrepreneurs, whose entrepreneurial spirit was awakened by the "Biti Bolji" program.

articles.title: Frano Šušnjara and Goran Šuša will talk to the students of Isidora Kršnjavog High School
articles.description: Frano Šušnjara, Group Managing Director of Stellantis for the Middle East, will visit the students of Isidor Kršnjavo High School in Našice...
articles.excerpt: Frano Šušnjara, Group Managing Director of Stellantis for the Middle East, will visit the students of Isidor Kršnjavo High School in Našice...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Association Biti Bolji i magazine Poduzetnik continue to bring famous and successful entrepreneurs and managers to Slavonian secondary schools. on Tuesday, December 20, 2022. students Secondary school of Isidor Kršnjavog in Našice will visit Frano Šušnjara, Group Managing Director at Stellantis for the Middle East i Goran Suša, owner of a consulting company let'Z talk C&B. 

The visit is being held as part of the "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project, which has been carried out in Croatia for nine years, as part of which more than 250 lectures have been held. About 150 guests visited the schools, and more than 38,000 students listened to all the activities.

Frano Šušnjara

Frano Šušnjara he was born and grew up in Senj. This successful manager is on the business path, as he says, since he was 26 years old as a manager, sales director and marketing director in the automotive industry. He worked at the very top of Renault in Croatia, Slovenia, France, Poland, Hong Kong, Brazil. Since 2021, he has been working in Paris, at Stellantis, one of the world's leading car manufacturers and mobility service providers, as Managing Director for Overseas Operations. Few people manage to break into the very top management of large companies, but Frano Šušnjara succeeded in this, and we are grateful to him for agreeing to tell the students how.

Goran Suša

Goran Suša He was born in Vinkovci, where he graduated from the High School of Economics, after which he went to Zagreb, where he graduated from the Faculty of Economics, majoring in Organization and Management. From the first working day, he focuses on HR, with specialization in organization, salary and reward systems. In 2011, he moved to France, to the headquarters of the Lactalis Group, where he held the positions of International Mobility manager and Compensation manager for the next six years. In 2017, he moved to Lille, where he assumed the position of Compensation & Benefit Leader for the Kiabi Group and remained there until his return to Croatia in the summer of 2020, when he assumed the position of Director of Strategic Human Resources Planning for the HT Group. In 2022, he opened his own consulting firm for strategic human resource management consulting, specializing in salary, reward and benefit policies and systems, and their strategic alignment with the vision, mission and strategy of both the HR department and the entire company.

Association Biti Bolji i magazine Poduzetnik continue to bring famous and successful entrepreneurs to Slavonian secondary schools. December 9, 2022. Dr. med. Biljana Ignatovska, specialist in radiology, owner and director of Polyclinic Arcadia, Daruvar.

The visit is being held as part of the "Biti Bolji - Be Better" project, which has been carried out in Croatia for nine years, as part of which more than 250 lectures have been held. About 150 guests visited the schools, and more than 40,000 students listened to all the activities.

About the guest:

dr. honey. Biljana Ignatovska, radiology specialist, claims that entrepreneurship chose her. In 2019, she took over the management position of Polyclinic Arcadia from her own father, aware that her position as a doctor and director must become equal in importance. In addition to the Arcadia Polyclinic, it also took over the family OPG, which grows hazelnuts.

"Whether inheriting a business is a gift or a burden, it's hard to say, I don't think too much about it. But I would rather say it's a gift because you don't have to start everything over again. I inherited an already established company that has been doing business successfully for more than 20 years. The burden is greater in the sense of introducing changes that reflect me and my personality among people who are used to working in a certain way. The burden is certainly also the feeling that you must not "mess up" something that has been working so successfully for a long time." she said in a conversation with Vladimir Mihajlović.

About the guest:

Daniel Ackermann he has been in business since the age of 15, and he started his first company at the age of 22, in 2009, during the worst recession. On your entrepreneurial journey, with your partner Tomislav Grubišić, he developed:

  • Degordian, a digital agency with 130 employees in several offices
  • Bornfight, software development a company with 80 employees
  • Mediatoolkit, media monitoring tool with 50 employees
  • Stethoscope, employee satisfaction and engagement tool

"I am extremely proud that no Croatian company in history has as many awards as our companies count today. Degordian is the winner of as many as six awards for the best employer, other companies have four more, for a total of ten awards. As a person, I am fulfilled by playing sports, running, painting, my dog Miko, I love to travel and eat", in last interview for Poduzetnik Daniel told us and added: "I think anyone can succeed. It's a matter of commitment, desire and mindset. I find Jack Ma's attitude very interesting (founder Alibaba) who says that you are not defined by what you do from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., but by what you do after 5 p.m. And then he listed more examples, like this: 'Marko was an architect and he was not satisfied with the chosen one. He was very attracted to digital design. He started studying. He was engaged in architecture during the day, and every evening he took courses and practiced UX. After a year, he got his first great UX job, and today, 10 years later, he leads design for a Fortune 500 company. And I completely agree with this. It's not important to be the smartest, it's important that you find your passion, that you really dedicate yourself to it and success will come."

articles.title: Autumn fair at Elementary School Budrovci
articles.description: Autumn Fair at Budrovci Elementary School, an activity within the European Entrepreneurship School project, which is organized in cooperation with Budrovci Elementary School...
articles.excerpt: Autumn Fair at Budrovci Elementary School, an activity within the European Entrepreneurship School project, which is organized in cooperation with Budrovci Elementary School...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
The autumn fair at Elementary School Budrovci, an activity within the project of the European School of Entrepreneurship, which is being held in cooperation with Elementary School Budrovci and the School of Economics "Braća Radić" for the sixth year in a row, was held on October 26, 2022.

Preparations began with a workshop in which students and teachers participated. The workshop was held by a project team of teachers from the "Braća Radić" School of Economics from Đakovo and students from training companies. The Republic of Croatia will introduce the euro as its official currency on January 1, 2023. At the moment, the focus is on dual reporting of prices and other monetary values ​​and their conversion. Dual reporting of prices is mandatory from September 5, 2022, so training companies are also adapting to market conditions.

Pupils and teachers of Elementary School Budrovci learned about the history of the euro, the European Central Bank (ESB), the introduction of the euro in the Republic of Croatia, the fixed kuna to euro conversion rate, dual pricing, dual circulation and in which denominations euro banknotes and coins will be printed. At the workshop, they learned to recalculate product prices and thus prepared for the upcoming fair.

The fair was held in the schoolyard and passed, as usual, in a happy and working atmosphere of students and teachers who diligently prepared for it. 

At the fair, which was held in a cheerful and working atmosphere in the schoolyard, this year small companies offereddomestic pickled pepper, cakes, pasta, jams, candied apples, natural freshly squeezed juices and products from nuts i cereals. This year, the offer was diverse, high-quality and aesthetically very attractive. The novelty at the fair was an offer freshly baked waffles and handmade bath soap, wooden jewelry and watches. The effort that students and teachers invested in preparing the fair was visible at every step and in the multitude of details that did not leave any visitor indifferent. All promotional materials were made according to the rules, everywhere the price was shown in euros. In addition to the preparation for the introduction of the euro, this year the emphasis was on the in-house production of all products.

By participating in the fair, the students got the opportunity to show their originality, creativity and communication and negotiation skills. It was a step by which students gained small but significant skills in managing personal finances and money in general. The students were very resourceful and prepared, and to the commission's question, "Can I pay for products in euros?", received the answer that this is only possible from January 1, 2023.

The number of visitors speaks volumes about the tradition of the eventAutumn fairimportant for the people of Budrov, the school, students, teachers, but also parents who are actively involved in all fair activities.

The fair was of a competitive nature, and the committee members who evaluated the companies were Memorial of Crnoja, Anamarija Geiger, Vesna Šimić, Jelica Paradžik-Lazarević i Tomislav Jurič.  

The company won the first place in the classroom teaching category Valuable hands (1st class), second place is shared by companies A happy group (3rd class), and the third place was taken by the company A little treat (4th grade).

The company won the first place in the classroom teaching category of the Đurđanci regional school Stars (3rd and 4th grade), the second place is shared by two companies Indians (1st class), and the third place was taken by the company Hedgehogs (2nd grade).

In the subject teaching category, the first place was won by the company Autumn spells (5th grade), the second place was the company 3, 2, 1 eat (8th grade) and placed third DPK (7th grade).

The title The most beautiful stand the company won A happy group. Praise for entrepreneurial innovation company Stars which offered handmade wall clocks, and for the entrepreneurial creativity of the KMT (Club of young technicians).

We are extremely proud of the cooperation between our schools and students who exchange and transfer experiences and entrepreneurial skills to each other. We hope that this cooperation will continue because we are rare, and perhaps even the only ones in the Republic of Croatia, who cooperate in this way. Our goal in the future is to raise their business to a higher level and introduce them to socially responsible business.

articles.title: How does entrepreneurship connect us?
articles.description: We found exactly such partners in the BHV Education company, which has been advising young people about studying abroad and building a career for 28 years.
articles.excerpt: We found exactly such partners in the BHV Education company, which has been advising young people about studying abroad and building a career for 28 years.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
It's wonderful to be surrounded by like-minded people. People who share our values, intellectual interests and the need to contribute to the betterment of the world.

We found exactly such partners in the company BHV Education which has been advising young people for 28 years about studying abroad and building a career. The joint initiative of this company and Associations Biti Bolji a comfortable bus was provided that brought students and teachers from Slavonia to Zagreb to the international conference and education fair "Mobility and Education Days 2022".

More than a thousand visitors were informed about the possibilities of studying abroad and talked with about fifty representatives of high schools, colleges, business schools and language schools from Austria, Italy, Slovenia, Spain, France, UK, Switzerland, Netherlands, Germany, Hungary, Czech Republic, America.

It was very dynamic, educational, but also fun. The lucky winners have been drawn in a prize draw for professional orientation, and we are still "crossing our fingers" that one of ours will be drawn in a very valuable prize draw in which BHV Education and the EF school award a language course in a city of their choice in Europe and a return plane ticket.

From an entrepreneurial perspective, we want to encourage you to consider continuing your education or training abroad, and these are our top reasons:

1. A challenge

Going to study abroad means leaving your comfort zone. You will have to study in a foreign language, adapt to a new culture, find new friends, organize your own work and free time, maybe even learn to cook. In this way, you will put yourself in fifth gear in terms of your academic and personal development and without any additional effort you will develop the qualities and behaviors that are necessary for success in entrepreneurship.

2. Modern education

Talking to Croatian students who are currently studying abroad or who have graduated, we found out that the decisive reason for their choice was a study program that is not available in our country. For example, in the Netherlands you can study "Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence", in England "Global Design Engineerig", in Switzerland "Marketing and Management for Luxury Tourism", to name just a few that are not available here. Of course, each educational institution has different admission requirements and tuition fees, but many of them are very affordable, or even free, and scholarships are also available. You can find out about all this at free consultations with BHV advisers.

3. Professional practice during studies

Employers joke (although they don't laugh) that they get people from Croatian universities with big heads full of information that they don't know what to do with. In order not to end up in that category of young employees, it is important to choose a course that will enable you to apply and question your theoretical knowledge in practice. Faculties abroad cooperate with companies and corporations of all sizes, which will enable you to make significant business contacts and find your first job more easily. In addition, when you experience working in a real environment, you will know what kind of work environment suits you best - small business or corporation, public or private, office work or flexible, a lot of business travel or a monotonous everyday life. You don't know until you experience it on your own skin.

4. Encouraging environment for starting your own business

Whatever you decide to study abroad, you will have the opportunity to meet guest lecturers from the real sector, innovators and investors who will use their knowledge and experience to inspire you to think outside the box and consider an entrepreneurial path. Did you know that international students are the founders of as many as 57% of startups founded at British universities?

5. Communication

Language is the basis of our communication, learning, collaboration and progress. By studying abroad, you will speak several foreign languages ​​fluently, perfect your public speaking and professional writing skills, all of which are prerequisites for success in your career, entrepreneurial or otherwise.

If you missed the live fair, do not miss the online fair that BHV Education is preparing on December 10, 2022. You can read about professional orientation, education abroad and everything that BHV Education offers athere.

articles.excerpt: SUPEUS, the Student Association for the Promotion of Energy Efficiency and Consulting, is organizing the 12th SUPEUS Case Study, which...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
SUPEUS, the Student Association for the Promotion of Energy Efficiency and Consulting, organizes 12. SUPEUS Case Study, which is held again after three years at three faculties (Af/Gf, FER and FSB), from October 24 to 26, through three two-part workshops: ARCHITECTURE / CONSTRUCTION, MECHANICAL ENGINEERING and ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING.

The announcement of the winner and the reception will be held in Friday, October 28, 2022, at the Faculty of Architecture.

Since prior knowledge is not necessary, the workshops are designed in such a way that in the first part, professors and experts will present the topic and hold a lecture where the participants will learn and learn everything they need to solve the task in the second part. Students, divided into teams, solve the task with prepared materials, instructions and technical support from the organizers.

It is possible to register individually (via "I'm looking for a team") or as a team (2-3 members) for one, two or all three workshops. This year's SCS is organized in such a way that the workshops continue with each other in order to encourage interdisciplinarity among students as much as possible, so the main prizes have been prepared for the teams that collect the most points through all three workshops. However, we especially value and reward the best solutions from individual workshops, so teams that compete in only one can compete in this category. Therefore, the awards are divided into two categories: the award for the best solution from a particular workshop and the main interdisciplinary awards. Regardless of how many workshops you participate in, all teams start the workshops equally.

More information about the project and applications are waiting for you HERE.

The theme of this year's SCS is "Energy renovation of a family house"

On the real example of a family house (Zagreb location), students will learn about the engineering approach to energy renovation. According to the determined state, they will analyze the possible measures and ultimately provide the optimal solution, which will bring the family house in question to the condition of an almost zero energy building. They will get closer to the students computer program KI Expert Plus for energy certification of buildings and creation of projects for rational use of energy and thermal protection of buildings. The idea is that each workshop works on the same project so that after the third day, i.e. after entering all the necessary data, an energy certificate can be obtained.                                  

Faculty of Architecture and Civil Engineering – "Contemporary Mantle"

Each hero in the story has his own mantle, and so does the house in the modern struggle to reduce energy consumption and CO2 emissions into the atmosphere. Join the workshop and discover how to create an optimal thermal mantle. But be careful, you will get a house with an existing envelope that requires a professional "update", has several conditions and wants only modern materials. Is it too demanding? It's not, with the help of the professor, the lecturer and our help, you will be able to give the heroine of this SCS story an initial jump towards a higher energy class. Come and prove that you have the best solution.

Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Shipbuilding – "Effective system"

The task with which we are going to SCS this year is related to the heating systems of our modest house. Your goal will be to choose the most efficient heating system and, according to it, determine other socio-ecological factors that may or may not have an impact on our environment. We will also ask you for a written explanation of why you used that system, your opinion on the effectiveness of the system and ways to improve it. We know, at first this seems complicated, but don't be afraid, we've made the task fun and adaptable for all comers.

Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing – "Independent house"

Do you know what photovoltaic systems are and how they work? In this workshop, you will learn what is needed to design a solar power plant on the roof of a family house - what parts a solar power plant consists of, how to properly dimension it, and how much is the initial investment and the investment return period. If this intrigued you, join us at this year's workshop.

articles.title: Biti Bolji – Be Better: Introducing students to interesting topics from the world of entrepreneurship
articles.description: As part of the project "Biti Bolji – Be Better" and elective classes in the subject of Entrepreneurship, on June 9, 2022, a visit was organized...
articles.excerpt: As part of the project "Biti Bolji – Be Better" and elective classes in the subject of Entrepreneurship, on June 9, 2022, a visit was organized...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
As part of the project "Biti Bolji - Be Better" and elective classes in the subject of Entrepreneurship, June 9, 2022 a visit of an entrepreneur and writer was organized Kristina Ercegović who gave a successful lecture to third graders XI. gymnasium in Zagreb.

The initiative for meeting and mutual cooperation was launched by the magazine Poduzetnik and the association Biti Bolji from Osijek. Students of XI. she introduced the high school students to interesting challenges and personal successes as well as the obstacles she encountered, all with the aim of motivating students to take the entrepreneurial path.

The guest started her lecture with basic knowledge of what entrepreneurship is in order to make the students more aware of the advantages and risks faced by entrepreneurs. The students and the guest discussed the most important topics relevant to starting their own business, and they also touched on the most famous and successful Croatian entrepreneurs. Kristina went on to talk about the importance of initial capital, and she also mentioned the case of a Croatian entrepreneur whose grandmother provided the initial capital necessary to start a business, thus emphasizing the importance of family support. Consequently, she was interested in whether the students' family members were also entrepreneurs.

One of the topics related to the harmonization of the business and private life of every entrepreneur, which represents a special challenge for women when they decide to marry and become mothers, emphasizing that the support of their partners is extremely important. The students were particularly interested in what are the first steps to be taken after a business idea that is planned to be implemented is conceived and how to choose the best option for a trading company. Depending on the nature of the work, one can choose to establish a company, whether it is about d.o.o. or j.d.o.o. or the entrepreneur can opt for a trade, flat-rate trade or association. The lecturer also mentioned the risks, problems and initial failures that entrepreneurs often face, but she also highlighted the positive sides, along with the persistence that is necessary to reach the goal and achieve success.

"Our esteemed guest, Kristina Ercegović, finished her lecture in an optimistic and cheerful tone, which will be an additional incentive for the young generations," said professor Jelena Lulić.

articles.title: Vladimir Mihajlović: "Young people are the ones who need to change the negative perception of entrepreneurs"
articles.description: Vladimir Mihajlović, editor-in-chief of Poduzetnik magazine, believes that it is young people who need to change the negative perception of...
articles.excerpt: Vladimir Mihajlović, editor-in-chief of Poduzetnik magazine, believes that it is young people who need to change the negative perception of...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
The members of the association 'Biti Bolji', led by Vladimir Mihajlović, know very well that the world rests on the young.editor-in-chief of Poduzetnik magazine.And that it should not be just a passing platitude, but a sentence that should lead us towards a better future, they show with their valuable activities that they want to inspire young people to start thinking about what they will do when they "grow up".

They are already at the very beginning of their project'Biti Bolji - Be Better'attracted the interest of many students and schools, and this only gave them the wind at their backs to continue spreading the 'voice of entrepreneurs' and to design even more interesting campaigns. So what made young people so interested and how did they turn serious topics into fun and interactive workshops that they will remember forever? Vladimir reveals to us below.

The association 'Biti Bolji' and the project 'Biti Bolji - Be Better', in collaboration with the magazine Poduzetnik, were born from the desire to encourage young people to think innovatively and engage in entrepreneurship. Can you tell us more about the very beginnings, did you expect to attract a large number of students?

- When we started an educational and creative project intended for young people, students of primary and secondary schools in Croatia, we did not know that we would attract a huge number of students and cover the whole of Croatia. The project was started by the magazine Poduzetnik, and then everything was continued by the Association 'Biti Bolji' from Osijek. Poduzetnik magazine is today the media sponsor of this project.

We knew that young people are creative, sometimes stubborn, but they go forward and bring what every society needs, new ideas, enthusiasm, smile and joy,that positive "craziness"… And that's nice. Young people drive every society. They are future scientists, professors, innovators, writers, artists, musicians, actors, athletes... but also future entrepreneurs who will start the economy.

Can you explain in more detail which activities you are trying to achieve this with?

- During each visit to the schools, before the start of the project, we held a presentation where we introduced the students and teachers to what we want to convey to them. They chose the activities they wanted after our suggestions and a survey questionnaire on students' attitudes towards entrepreneurship and education. We did not impose anything on the students.Through conversations, workshops, lectures, forums, research, holding concerts and plays, visits to entrepreneurs and other various events, the students were the ones who determined a series of topics that we realized through various activities.

I'll just listsome of these activities:Being an entrepreneur/manager; Being a woman in entrepreneurship; Green is best; Socially responsible business; Life without money; Let's discover ourselves; I want to be; Youth and today's challenges; Youth in the EU; Digitization in life and business; I volunteer, I value, I value - What can I do for my community; Let's create a comic; Student research; Mentoring of talented students... and a number of other activities.

How many students and schools have joined the 'Biti Bolji - Be Better' project so far?

- We managed to include entrepreneurs, the local community, institutions that support entrepreneurship, interesting famous people and of course students and professors in the project. Since the beginning of the project, we have visited about 50 primary and secondary schools (some more than once) and several colleges in Croatia.

More than 38,000 students listened to us directly, and about 50,000 students indirectly. After visiting so many students, we can freely say that young people are capable of achieving anything, they are better than we think. We learned that they are full of energy, innovative, creative, and theirsthe desire to succeedis endless.

So far, you have held over 200 workshops for students. What do they look like? What activities do students enjoy the most?

- Yes, more than 200 activities were held, 150 people who visited the schools got involved. We visited schools in Osijek, Đakovo, Valpovo, Našice, Vukovar, Vinkovci, Donji Miholjec, Beli Manastir, Požega, Varaždin, Virovitica, Prelog, Ivanec, Ivanić Grad, Bjelovar, Kutina, Split, Antunovac, Gunja, Rokovci, Babina Greda,...

All activities were set up so that the conversation with the guest was closer to the students, simply,interesting and understandable.And of course, students are directly involved in the activity. Our relationship with the students was based on the 'Why-Why' relationship. Countless questions were asked by the students, to which they received answers.

Did you get a specific onefeedbackstudents after the visits?

- After each visit, students wrote to us about how they experienced that visit. We felt their satisfaction, especially because they were present "from the inside" in every activity. The satisfaction is even greater because we continue to visit schools in Croatia.

As an example, I will cite a letter from a student of Zvjezdana: "Through an interesting way and conversation, we got to know the world of entrepreneurs. It was very fun, but also interesting and instructive. I would especially like to highlight the editorof the magazine Poduzetnikwho showed us how the magazine works. And I was especially impressed by the fact that we were all involved in the presentation."

Can you already see at the workshops who could one day become their own boss, and who would still be more satisfied working for someone else?

– You may not see it directly, but you can feel the spirit of the students. Many want to be their own boss, but they are not sufficiently informed and educated on how to become one and what it means to be their own boss. That is why it is the special role of the school and all of us who are in business to support students in all the ways available to them. Our duty is to organize specific workshops on this topic.

I would say that most high school students are quiet, they want to work for someone else with a decent income and conditions that will allow them as much and varied free time as possible. They say:"Work is not the only meaning of life."It is interesting how elementary school students react more freely and spontaneously. They spout questions, there's nothing they don't want to know. The most important thing we heard in secondary schools boils down to: more practice, less theory. Travel more. Visit and meet entrepreneurs. Ask them questions.

As part of the project, the campaign "Every Student Entrepreneur" was created. What kind of activities are carried out here? What is the goal of the campaign?

- At every meeting with the students, I used to say: "Opportunity is bald from behind!" In a figurative sense, it means that once an opportunity passes, it is difficult to seize it, so when it appears again - take advantage of it.

After two or three years, professors-coordinators and students from schools started contacting us saying that they use the magazine Poduzetnik in their classes. Their communication was the impetus for the campaign we launched last year called: 'Every student is an entrepreneur'.

Through this campaign, we want to enable each school and college to receive an annual grant through donorssubscriptions to the magazine Poduzetnik, which currently receives about 400 primary and secondary schools in Croatia. And of course, let's move on!

Do you have a certain system by which you choose the schools to which you will donate subscriptions to the magazine Poduzetnik? In case an individual wants to become a donor, can he choose the desired school or does he leave the choice to you?

- A donor can be anyone who wants to get involved, an entrepreneur, an institution, a local government, a natural person... Just about everyone. The donor can choose the primary and secondary schools in Croatia to which he wishes to donate an annual subscription to the magazine Poduzetnik, and we will inform the schools who the donor is.

They can leave the choice of schools to us. Support can also be through a recommendation to business partners as an invitation to join the project. There are 919 primary schools, 439 secondary schools and 212 higher education institutions and public universities, private universities and colleges operating in Croatia. Our goal is to enable all schools in Croatia to receive the magazine Poduzetnik.

You can read more about the campaignon the link.

In addition to donating subscriptions, you also organize visits by entrepreneurs to schools. Who has already had the opportunity to transfer their knowledge and experience to students?

– A series of lecturers and guests,from entrepreneurs to public figures, visited schools and shared their experiences with students. Among them were Goran Milić, a well-known journalist; Krešimir Mišak, host of the TV show "On the edge of science"; Đelo Hadžiselimović, famous editor of HTV; Mirsada Kudrić, general director of Bosch Croatia; Drago Munjiza, manager; Jako Andabak, entrepreneur; Boris Mikšić, an entrepreneur from the USA; Nenad Bach, musician from the USA; Neno Belan and Olja Dešić, famous musicians; Žarko Radulović, owner of Hotel Splendid from Budva; Mufti Dr. Aziz ef. Hasanović, Islamic community in Croatia.

Miro Gavran, a famous writer, was also there; Ivan Gudelj, legendary football player of Hajduk; Zijah Sokolović, famous actor; Bernarda Cecelja, owner and director of Bernarda d.o.o. from Nedelišće; Vitomir Klasić, Ivanićplast from Ivanić Grad; Ivan Bračić, owner of PIP d.o.o. from Pisarovina; Alan Honan, one of two brothers from Ireland who left Ireland and started a business in Croatia; Frano Šušnjara managing director for Overseas operations in Stellantis; Thomas Bauer, co-owner andchief content creatoragency Grizli komunikacije d.o.o. from Zagreb; Zlatko Rabik, an entrepreneur from Slatina,

We also invited entrepreneurs such as Ognjen Bagatin from Polyclinic Sinteza; Siniša Marijan, President of the Končar-Institute of Electrical Engineering Zagreb; Ivo Bilić, Kentbank d.d. Zagreb; Gordana Deranja, owner of the company Tehnomont Pula; Darija Mateljak, Hauska & Partner from Zagreb and many othersentrepreneurs, managers and public figuresfrom all over Croatia.

In addition, you even organized some concerts and plays? Do you have any new guest appearances planned for the upcoming school year?

- That's right, in Osijek we organized a concert by Nena Belan, Olje Dešić and Nenad Bach for students. For students from Slavonia, we organized 9 theater performances by Zijah Sokolović and the Mala scena theater from Zagreb for free.

We also took the students on several visits to entrepreneurs: the Tehnomont Pula shipyard (owned by Gordana Deranja); shoe factory Zlatna nit Slatina; Končar d.d. – two visits, Bernarda d.o.o. Nedelišće - mattress, bed and pillow factory (owner Bernarda Cecelj).

We continue on, and I hereby thank everyone for taking their timefree timeto talk to young people. The school visit plan with guests is completed by the end of the year, it remains for us to agree with the schools in the fall, at the beginning of the school year, the details of the visit.

In your opinion, how else can young people influence the creation of their own future? In what profiles of students are future entrepreneurs hiding, what qualities should they already possess?

- Regardless of expectations, it is young people who "must" create their future, of course with our support. 9 years ago, the professions for which they were trained were 'usual'. The future is looking for new occupations related to new technologies, the IT sector, artificial intelligence, some of them are yet to come, but what is especially necessary isencouraging studentsto craft occupations.

Learning never stops, the school will give them the foundations, and everything else is self-interest, a lot of work, creativity, informal acquisition of knowledge and skills, volunteering, learning by trial and error. Let them already think about what they will do in the future. Young people are the ones who need to change the negative perception of entrepreneurs.

The valuable work of the association was also recognized by the company Tokić with a generous donation. Do you already know what activities and new workshops will be useful for you?

- Yes, the company Tokić d.o.o. she recognized our work. We were at their place for a conversation and we immediately came to a common conclusion that our focus is the same: young people. We look forward to cooperation with company Tokić and thank you for recognizing the work of the Association 'Biti Bolji' and supporting the youth project 'Biti Bolji - Be Better'.

Thanks to the receipt of their valuable donation, we will be able to implement future projects more easily and thus encourage themexpansion of entrepreneurialmindsetamong young peoplewho are our future and from whom everything begins. I want to emphasize that the Tokić company approved a one-day visit to their headquarters in Sesvete, so in the fall we are taking 50 students there. And of course, we are very proud of this.

In what ways can we get involved and support the work of your association?

- Anyone who wants to can support the work of the Association 'Biti Bolji' by donating according to their means, by visiting one of the schools in Croatia, by inviting us to visit their company, by recommending them to business partners.

Call us on your cell phone091/767 5 999 or 091/600 80 52or by email:bitibolji4@gmail.com. Our joint commitment is to encourage the spread of an entrepreneurial mindset among young people who are our future and from whom everything starts.

On occasion of the ceremonial opening of the new Tokić branches in Đakovo, the local community also donated on occasion. articles.title: The magazine Poduzetnik and the Association "Biti Bolji" organize the visit of Frana Šušnjara and Thomas Bauer to the high school in Kutina
articles.description: On April 27, Frano Šušnjara and Thomas Bauer will visit the Tin Ujević high school in Kutina to introduce the students to top business topics.
articles.excerpt: On April 27, Frano Šušnjara and Thomas Bauer will visit the Tin Ujević high school in Kutina to introduce the students to top business topics.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Frano Šušnjara, managing director for Overseas operations at Stellantis and Thomas Bauer, co-owner and chief content creator of the agency Grizli komunikacije d.o.o. Zagreb, come to visit Kutina.

The visit is held as part of the project "Biti Bolji-Be Better" which takes place in Croatia for eight years. During the project, more than 130 lectures were held, with about 130 guests, and more than 35,000 students listened to all the activities.

On April 27, Frano Šušnjara and Thomas Bauer will visit the Tin Ujević high school in Kutina, and discuss the topics of entrepreneurship, management and market communication.

When: April 27, 2022 (Wednesday) from 10:45 a.m. to 12:20 p.m.
Where: Tino Ujević High School, Kutina
Who: Frano Šušnjara in conversation – Being a manager/entrepreneur (45 min), and Thomas Bauer in conversation – Market communication/Being an entrepreneur (45 min)

Who is Frano Šušnjara?

Born and raised in Senj. Worked at Renault in Croatia, Slovenia, France, Poland, Hong Kong, Brazil as marketing director or sales director. From 2021 again in Paris but in Stellantis as Managing Director for Overseas Operations.

Few people manage to break into the very top management of large companies. Frano Šušnjara succeeded, and we are grateful to him for agreeing to tell the students how. He spent most of his childhood in Senj, and later in Algeria, Romania and Albania. As far as education is concerned, he graduated from the Faculty of Political Sciences in Zagreb and an MBA from Cotrugli. He is happily married and a proud father.

Every country, every city has its own challenges, adaptation needs and difficulties in them. Different cultures, legal frameworks, customs and languages ​​are a feature of every society, so adaptation requires a certain amount of effort and persistence. I think that this need for a "reset" and permanent learning with great persistence is something that is woven into everyday life for many.

Frano Šušnjara

Croatia's branding is not just a jersey, prosciutto or a UNESCO plaque on a monument. It is something much deeper, more precise, something that requires time, professional work and effort in order to clearly define the value and uniqueness that we can offer behind the term Croatia, according to Frano.

Who is Thomas Bauer?

Thomas Bauer is a copywriter and creative director with many years of experience in the market communications industry, including 10 years at the agency Grizli komunikacije Zagreb, where he is co-owner and chief content creator. Behind him are numerous successful campaigns, professional awards and dozens of clients from various industries. He graduated in Geography at the Faculty of Arts in Zagreb and is not a professor by profession, but he has never worked in the profession.

The founders of the agency were among the first in the country to understand that content is king, and different forms of market communications are just his armies to subjugate the volatile market of the stagnant Croatian economy.

"After high school in Križanićeva, I enrolled in a college for which, after staring at atlases, I literally didn't study for a second. The Diploma in Geography at PMF directed my career towards demography, which I dealt with for over 5 years at the State Statistical Office. The civil service did not excite me, to put it mildly, and I decided to replace it with the private sector, numbers with letters, and Excel Word. I started working as a copywriter at the agency Bruketa i Žinić and as her part of me learning a new trade and winning numerous domestic and international awards and recognitions.

After seven years, which is quite a long period in a large advertising agency, together with a friend from Dinamo's fan stand, Tom Čehulić, I am starting Grizli. We opened a small agency, intended for small and medium-sized businesses, and as all this took place in the severe recession of 2012, versatility, flexibility and adaptability to different market conditions and challenges emerged as a comparative advantage of Grizzli.

Our special specialty is guerilla marketing, actually just a strategic form of thinking that can be applied with the help of various communication tools. For this purpose, we are building a young, almost kindergarten team from the beginning, because practically all Grizzli employees, except Tom and I, came to the agency directly from college."

articles.description: The "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project of the Osijek association Biti Bolji encourages young people to give their best and get involved in entrepreneurship.
articles.excerpt: The "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project of the Osijek association Biti Bolji encourages young people to give their best and get involved in entrepreneurship.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Central State Office for Demography and Youth In 2020, he approved the co-financing of activities in the "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project, which is implemented by the Biti Bolji Association from Osijek.

Due to the outbreak of the pandemic caused by the coronavirus, the project was not held in 2020 as planned but, with the approval of the Central State Office for Demography and Youth, was held in 2021, i.e. at the very end of the 2020/2021 school year. The priority areas for co-financing are "Increasing knowledge, skills and competitiveness on the labor market and encouraging social inclusion" and "Training for (social) entrepreneurship and self-employment."

Workshops Ecologically aware tourist and Being a woman in entrepreneurship

On June 15, Tamara Drezner held the "Ecologically Conscious Tourist" workshop for 18 students at the Ivan Domac Vinkovci School of Economics and Commerce. The aim of this workshop was to make students aware of socially responsible behavior towards the environment and to inform them about the advantages and principles of long-term sustainable eco-tourism in the world and in the Republic of Croatia. She held the workshop "Being a woman in entrepreneurship" on June 16 at the Osijek School of Economics and Administration for 16 students and on June 17 at the Braća Radić Đakovo School of Economics for 19 students with the aim of inspiring them to engage in entrepreneurship in the future and to inform them about the available supports intended for young entrepreneurs.

Workshop "Being a socially responsible entrepreneur"

On June 16, two workshops "Being a socially responsible entrepreneur" were held at the Osijek School of Economics and Administration for 63 students, and were held by Ognjen Bagatin, co-owner Polyclinic Bagatin and majority owner of Poduzetnik magazine.

The same workshops were held on June 17 at the Osijek School of Applied Art and Design for 36 students and at the Braća Radić Đakovo School of Economics for 19 students.

Ognjen Bagatin explained to the students how to use the knowledge learned in theory in practice and how to access the labor market more easily, how to be young and enterprising, how to be and remain creative. He supported all of the above with his own example and was happy to answer the students' questions.

Educational program "Biti Bolji“

From June 23 to 25, a three-day workshop was held for 10 gifted students, at the suggestion of the school, who showed a desire for education on the basics of entrepreneurship and who tried to apply the acquired knowledge to create a business plan with their ideas. The workshop consisted of three modules, each of which lasted eight school hours, and was attended by a total of 10 students from these schools: School of Economics and Administration Osijek, School of Economics and Trade Ivan Domca Vinkovci, School of Applied Art and Design, Technical School and Science High School Ruđer Bošković Osijek. The workshop was led by Tomislav Lneniček, and Vladimir Mihajlović also participated in one part of the lecture. Students had the opportunity to get acquainted with the basics of entrepreneurship and terms related to entrepreneurship. They learned how to develop their entrepreneurial idea and how to implement it. Through the workshop, participants were enabled to become aware of myths and prejudices about entrepreneurship and to adopt basic economic concepts and basic marketing and sales strategies.

Conclusion

The students of five high schools participated in the mentioned activities: Osijek School of Economics and Administration, Ivan Domca Vinkovci School of Economics and Trade, School of Applied Art and Design, Ruđer Bošković Technical School and Science High School Osijek, Braća Radić Đakovo School of Economics.

8 workshops were held

  • Educational program "Biti Bolji", lecturers Tomislav Lneniček and Vladimir Mihajlović, 10 students.

• Lecturer: Tamara Drezner, 3 workshops, 53 students.

  • Ecologically aware tourist, 1 workshop, 18 students
  • Being a woman in entrepreneurship, 2 workshops, 35 students

• Lecturer: Ognjen Bagatin, 4 workshops, 118 students.

  • Being a socially responsible entrepreneur, 4 workshops.

A total of 181 students participated in 8 activities/workshops.

Finally - a treat!

The last activity of this project is a study trip to Pula, where students, accompanied by professors and project organizers, visited the company Technomont d.d., headed by the President of the Management Board, Gordana Deranja. The company is oriented towards the construction of patrol, tourist, fishing and firefighting ships for the wide world market, and also deals with the overhaul of existing ships and the production of solar collectors for water heating, as well as nautical tourism - Marina Veruda. The trip was realized from July 15 to 17, 2021.

articles.title: Mobile application YEStivo coming soon!
articles.description: Today, the Association Biti Bolji signed an agreement with Osijek-Baranja County on the allocation of funds for the development of the YEStivo application.
articles.excerpt: Today, the Association Biti Bolji signed an agreement with Osijek-Baranja County on the allocation of funds for the development of the YEStivo application.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Today, the Association Biti Bolji s Osijek-Baranja county signed the contract on the allocation of funds for the creation of the application edible, all within the project idea Smart villages.

As part of the Biti Bolji - Be better project, which is aimed at young people and entrepreneurship, we started creating a mobile application called YEStivo, which aims to connect producers of agricultural food and other products and buyers of their products. The project was recognized by Osijek-Baranja County which, as part of the new concept of rural development, awarded this project idea a prize in the amount of HRK 10,000.00.

Through the location that is collected via a mobile device, the application shows the user all the manufacturers in his vicinity and under the manufacturer's profile it shows him all his products and information about them, as well as information about the manufacturer. Through the application, the customer can order his products and arrange to pick up the products from the manufacturer. The application in a special way digitizes the way of sale and communication between producers and buyers of goods.

The application has no geographical restrictions, but provides the possibility of displaying data within a certain distance radius from the customer himself, thus providing the possibility for the customer to find the nearest manufacturer of the desired product at any time during the trip. We will start with the Osijek-Baranja county, and in a later phase we will focus on other counties as well. The goal is to involve as many existing or new young producers as possible in the project.

The development of the application is planned to start at the beginning of February 2021, and it will take 6 months to create it. The total value of the project is HRK 70,000.00.

We expect help from the local government/self-government and other institutions and entities in promoting registration in the database.

We invite secondary schools from Osijek-Baranja County and the whole of Croatia to include students (classes) in the project, i.e. the creation of a manufacturer's database, which we will reward at the end. Also, we want to include in the project 3-5 talented students who have tendencies towards digital competences, and who will be able to participate in the development of the application from the beginning to the end of the project. Thus, we will be mentors to these students and give them the opportunity to become independent for future projects.

Please support our project with a donation/sponsorship so that the application will come to life in practice as soon as possible. Contact us via e-mail bitibolji4@gmail.com.

articles.content:
In compliance with all prescribed epidemiological measures, and to the great satisfaction of all stakeholders of this educational project, the youth project "Biti Bolji - Be Better" entered schools again this fall, for the eighth year in a row.

Poduzetnik Zlatko Rabik from Slatina, on September 25, 2020, he was a guest at the "Braća Radić" School of Economics in Đakovo. He held a lecture entitled "Being an entrepreneur" on the topic of production and sale of footwear and leather goods, which was organized by a project team consisting of teachers Anamarija Gajger, Marija Milanović, Spomenka Crnoja, Bernardica Šušak and Darinka Rechner.

Mr. Zlatko was already a guest at our school in May 2019, when he told the students how their family dream had become a successful business, but he also pointed out that the decisions to be made when choosing one's life calling and profession are not at all easy. Today's visit was a continuation of his entrepreneurial story. Zlatko Rabik, owner of the company Zlatna nit d.o.o., has 25 years of entrepreneurial experience, and all these years he went through difficult and easy periods in business and life.

Golden thread is a family company whose main activity is the production of footwear and the sale of HTZ equipment. Through twenty-five years of private entrepreneurship experience in the companies Toping and Zlatna nit, they managed to win their place on the market and survive in a very difficult and economically demanding environment. During this period, they had ups and downs, they developed from a small family business that started working in a garage, and in a short time they built a new factory of 800 m with their own capital.2 and 50 employees and continuously worked on the development of new products, fashion collections of youth, women's and men's footwear, and recently work and safety footwear.

"We follow technological progress and the needs of the market. We learn and acquire knowledge from various fields and apply it in our work. Last year, we put on and equipped over 7,000 workers in more than 400 companies, trades, OPG and institutions with work protective equipment. For almost ten years, we have been following a business plan and going directly to customers!", said Zlatko.

We learned something new

One part of the lecture was dedicated to students of the 1st grade in the sales profession under the dual system of education, because one of the subjects the students have is Footwear and Leather Goods. For the purpose of equipping the school practicum, Mr. Zlatko brought various types of natural leather, textile and artificial materials, soles, semi-finished products and finished shoes that the students will use for practice in the practicum. We are very grateful to him for that.

• Student Martina Šarac (1st grade, sales major): "Mr. Zlatko Rabik gave us a lecture on footwear and leather goods and on the production of footwear itself. Two hours was too little, but we found out and learned a lot. Mr. Zlatko is an entrepreneur who experienced a terrible economic downturn, but luckily he rose again and moved forward. He brought us several types of leather for samples - natural and artificial. When I asked how difficult it is to make one pair of shoes, he answered that it is difficult to that you need a lot of knowledge, but if you have the necessary materials and the will, everything is easier."

At the end of this lecture, the students were given refreshing drinks donated by Coca-Cola HBC Croatia.

articles.title: The ecological project "Biti Bolji-Be Better" has been completed
articles.description: The environmental project "Biti Bolji-Be Better", a project realized in the period from September 2019 to mid-March 2020, has been completed.
articles.excerpt: The environmental project "Biti Bolji-Be Better", a project realized in the period from September 2019 to mid-March 2020, has been completed.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
As part of Ina's program Green belt, the association "Biti Bolji" realized six basic activities in which the students of two elementary schools were involved - Tino Ujević Elementary School from Osijek and Nikola Andrić Elementary School from Vukovar.

After almost eight months since the beginning of the project, we can be really proud of all the students, professors and project sponsor Ina and her program Green belt, who, together with members of the Association "Biti Bolji" from Osijek, participated in a project that contributed to the preservation of the environment in local communities. The project in which we included students from two elementary schools was selected from last year's 16 winning projects.

What have we done?

The project was implemented in the period from September 2019 to mid-March 2020, and through it we:

  • Met 46 students of Tino Ujević Elementary School in Osijek and Nikola Andrić Elementary School in Vukovar with the project and planned activities.
  • Did a demonstration planting of 18 ecological fruit seedlings in the yard of Tin Ujević school in Osijek.
  • Held a lecture on the method of planting in a part of the school yard on an area of 200 m2.
  • Provided professional support and advice on the maintenance of seedlings for the duration of this project. The lecture, demonstration planting and professional support was provided by Dominik Vuković from the Fruit Growing Department of the Osijek Agricultural Institute.
  • Acquired the necessary tools and equipment for planting organic fruit seedlings.
  • Held two workshops called "How to be an informed tourist?" for a total of 41 students. The workshop was held by Tamara Drezner, an entrepreneur from Osijek.

"In cooperation with the Association 'Biti Bolji' and thanks to the financial support of INA, the students of the seventh grade planted 18 ecological fruit trees of apples, plums, sour cherries and cherries in the school yard. This experience remained in their very fond memories, and the opportunity to participate in a useful initiative raised the students' awareness of the need to protect the environment. Caring for fruit trees encourages and develops good habits, as well as making environmentally positive decisions in life. Also, in this way, the students' awareness is raised the quality of living in accordance with the preservation of nature and the environment", said Tihana Kraml Kanaet, teacher of mathematics and physics from Tina Ujević Elementary School.

"As the project leader, the Association 'Biti Bolji' from Osijek wanted to raise the level of environmental awareness and the adoption of healthy habits among the students of these elementary schools. Together with the students of Tino Ujević Primary School, we decorated part of their school yard by planting fruit seedlings, and through two workshops we introduced the students to the protection of the environment and nature and how to behave responsibly towards nature. We are especially grateful to our sponsor Come on and her program Green belt“, he said Vladimir Mihajlović, president of the Association.

articles.title: How to be an environmentally conscious tourist?
articles.description: At the workshop, we taught 6th grade students how to behave responsibly towards themselves and the environment, how to leave a positive mark on the environment we travel to.
articles.excerpt: At the workshop, we taught 6th grade students how to behave responsibly towards themselves and the environment, how to leave a positive mark on the environment we travel to.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
With the aim of spreading awareness about the importance of sustainable development, INA launched the program in 2014 Green belt within which she invited the cooperation of civil society organizations, public educational institutions (schools, kindergartens, colleges), voluntary fire brigades and nature parks in order to jointly contribute to the preservation of the environment in local communities.

Members of the association Biti Bolji Osijek continued to carry out activities within the project "Biti Bolji-Be Better", which INA chose for Green belt 2019. This time, Tamara Drezner, owner of PanadriaFly - a travel agency from Osijek, held a workshop for 18 students of Nikola Andrić Vukovar Primary School.

At the workshop, students of 6th grade B learned how to behave responsibly towards themselves and the environment, how to travel and leave a positive mark on the environment they travel to, what are the advantages of ecological tourism that is encouraged in Croatia and how we can preserve the environment together. The purpose of the workshop is for students to understand how we can all protect the planet and be environmentally aware, it just takes a little effort. The beginning of caring for the environment and the quality of our life on earth begins with interest and information about the environment, the principles of ecological tourism and the ecological state of the country.

The participants of the workshop learned the meaning of the terms ecology, the difference between a socially responsible traveler and a tourist, the positive effects of ecological tourism on the Croatian economy, the principles of ecological tourism and climate challenges related to global warming. The students had the opportunity to learn about the effects of traffic on the quality of the air we breathe, whether it is road or air traffic, and what steps transport companies take to preserve the environment and improve the quality of air and life on earth.

At the workshops, students were encouraged through dialogue to actively reflect on how they can preserve the environment through their daily behavior at home and on trips, for example by disposing of waste and conserving natural resources. They also had the opportunity to learn more about destination marketing through tourism and realistic images of destinations threatened by mass tourism. We hope that we have encouraged them to think about respect for nature, behavior at home and on excursions, the advantages of eco-friendly accommodation and transportation, joint planting of trees at school, garbage collection at school, and the like.

The workshop ended with an interactive crossword in which the participants, divided into groups, went over terms related to ecology, ecotourism, ecosystem or ecosystem, ecologically sustainable tourism and the principles of ecological tourism.

articles.title: Elementary School Tin Ujević Osijek: How to be an informed tourist?
articles.description: Tamara Drezner, as part of the Green Belt program, held a workshop for students entitled "How to be an environmentally conscious tourist?"
articles.excerpt: Tamara Drezner, as part of the Green Belt program, held a workshop for students entitled "How to be an environmentally conscious tourist?"
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Association Biti Bolji continued with the planned activities within the program Green belt which she co-financed INA for ecological projects and education about awareness and nature protection. This time, together with Tamara Drezner, we visited 22 seventh-grade students of Elementary School Tin Ujević Osijek. She held a workshop for students entitled "How to be an environmentally aware tourist?".

Tamara Drezner, owner and director of the travel agency PanadriaFly, on February 26, 2020, she gave a lecture to the students of Tin Ujević Elementary School in Osijek. Tamara spoke about the ecological awareness of tourists, that is, about how we can contribute to the preservation of nature, the environment and the cities we visit as tourists. The first step towards the protection of all natural beauty and everything that the inhabitants of a place have created with their efforts and work is socially responsible behavior. Such behavior implies respect for the culture and customs of the place where we come, because we are tourists and do not stay long, and the local people are left with everything we leave behind and how we behave. The way we behave at home and in our town or city is the behavior we should "bring" to the place we visit.

One of the biggest problems of tourism, which is growing day by day, is mass tourism. Mass visits to tourist attractions, natural beauties and habitats of plant and animal life will lead to their destruction. For this reason, each of us must carry a part of responsibility and cultural behavior towards the environment during tourist visits.

Tamara gave advice to elementary school students on how to behave on student excursions and encouraged them to think about what environmentally responsible behavior should really be. The students came to conclusions so that they could contribute to the preservation of ecology in the role of tourists, and they also participated in a workshop in which they repeated everything they heard in the lecture through an interesting crossword puzzle and thus established their knowledge about environmentally conscious behavior in tourism.

articles.title: Young people are our future
articles.description: It is important for young people to understand already at secondary school age that they can be creators of their future and employers, and not just passive observers...
articles.excerpt: It is important for young people to understand already at secondary school age that they can be creators of their future and employers, and not just passive observers...
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
It is important that young people already in high school understand how they can be creators of their future, and not just passive observers - employers who will hire, not just employees in companies. Young people are our future and only they can contribute to the stronger economic development of the country in the long term - is the opinion of Gordana Deranja, the first woman in charge Croatian Association of Employers, president of the Tehnomont Shipyard Management Board from Pula, entrepreneur and manager who holds the title for many years manager of the year.

As part of the Biti Bolji project, Gordana Deranja visited two schools

As part of the project "Biti Bolji-Be Better" she visited two schools, on May 9, 2019, the Hospitality and Tourism School Osijek, where the lecture was attended by 70 students, and on May 10, the Ivan Domac Vinkovci School of Economics and Commerce, where 50 final year students of this school, as well as other interested people, had the opportunity to hear her.

I want that in the future it will not matter who is a woman and who is a man, but what knowledge and competence someone has and how well they know how to do their job. Something drastic needs to change in order for us to be better off, and I hope that you are the young hope of Croatia, the future entrepreneurs, who will change the future of our economy. - said Gordana Deranja to the students, stressing that knowledge is extremely important and that they should never stop learning. She encouraged them to develop their creativity and communication and to learn to be team players who will know how to deal with victories and defeats.

Gordana Deranja told the students about the importance of starting a business, which may sometimes not work out as we imagined, but that is not a shame. Deranja showed by her example that you can succeed when you have a goal and persistence in life.

The importance of starting a business - Thomas Bauer

The association "Biti Bolji" and the magazine Poduzetnik also organized a visit by Thomas Bauer, director of the company Grizli komunikacije from Zagreb. On May 17, Thomas and his colleague Lara Levak visited the Varaždin School of Economics, where he held an interesting interactive lecture on market communication for about 40 students and several professors.

He talked about communication on social networks, about good and bad ads and the differences between them. We found out which channels of communication are important and how crucial emotions are in communication and why most people prefer a certain brand.

Thomas told the students that many companies in our country still do not understand the importance of market communication and that they have to allocate part of the money, that is, invest in advertising, because it is an investment, not an expense. We have seen several commercials on a global level that really evoked emotions in everyone present. "We were among the first to realize that content is the key and very important for market communication, and whether you want to tell the story through billboards, TV commercials, interviews in PR or social networks is another question."

Not only the students were satisfied with this lecture, but also the present professors who recognized that this topic is interesting and for a special lecture for them. Why not?! – replied Thomas Bauer.

Thank you to our guest entrepreneurs for supporting the "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project and taking their precious time to introduce themselves to the students and encourage them to think about entering the world of entrepreneurship. We are aware that knowledge is priceless, but also that it is sometimes difficult to acquire and adopt. That is why every new knowledge is of inestimable value to these young people and can bring great changes in the life of each of them.

articles.title: A story of personal development and success
articles.description: Zoran Salopek, a well-known and successful entrepreneur from Zagreb, held lectures in schools as part of the "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project.
articles.excerpt: Zoran Salopek, a well-known and successful entrepreneur from Zagreb, held lectures in schools as part of the "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
One of the goals of the project is to develop and strengthen entrepreneurial competencies among students based on concrete examples of good practice, which will result in the acquisition of additional knowledge and skills necessary for the future. "Biti Bolji-Be Better".

You need to induce happiness, you need to make a step forward in order to make something happen - these are the words of Zoran Salopek, today's well-known and successful entrepreneur from Zagreb, who says that leaving his comfort zone was crucial for his success. Zoran gladly accepted our proposal and without much thought answered the invitation and supported our project "Biti Bolji-Be Better" and shared his life and entrepreneurial experiences with the students.

Guest of two schools

U Agricultural school in Zagreb, we were enthusiastically welcomed by the principal, Mr. Ivica Marinić, especially Zoran, who himself was a student of this school. He chose to talk to the students of this school for this very reason. The students involved in the school project "Small Academy of Young Farmers" participated with great interest in the interactive lecture, where they received many wise tips that will help them on their life's journey. Also, there were several professors who showed great interest in Zoran's lecture.

U Secondary school "Ban Josip Jelačić" in Zaprešić, we were welcomed by the project coordinator, prof. Sabina Potočnjak with about 50 students who listened attentively to Zoran's story about personal development and success.

Zoran told the students about his not-so-easy school life. In his teenage days, when the point of an individual is to stand out from the crowd, Zoran did just that. He wasn't ashamed to admit that he didn't know something and didn't blend in with the crowd, even though many criticized him for it. He said that most people draw conclusions based on their emotions and that is why they should question, learn, work and fight. But it is important to know why something is being done and to have a goal.

He told how he traveled around 60 countries without a 'kinta' in his pocket, only with a backpack on his back. Through these trips, he realized that he can live a little better, but also a lot worse. He recommended the students to travel the world in order to build themselves, gain a lot of knowledge and courage because not all answers can be found in books.

We are all building a skyscraper of life's achievements

Self-criticism is a very important trait - said Zoran, and added that the key factors for success are dedicated work, good education, and happiness should be caused by leaving the comfort zone. In the end, he told the young people that failure is part of success and that they should not be afraid to try. We all build a skyscraper of our life's achievements, and Zoran translated his achievements into the book "The Skyscraper of Life".
