INA as part of her company's social responsibility, recognized the importance of environmental projects and education and raising awareness among young people about nature protection, so as part of the program Green belt decided to finance many "green" projects. Association Biti Bolji from Osijek was given the opportunity to participate in the competition Inina financial help to realize their plans, so on December 13, 2019, in the yard of Tino Ujević Primary School in Osijek, together with seventh grade students, members of the Association beautified the school garden with apple, plum, cherry and cherry seedlings.

With a professional the help of Mr. Dominik Vuković from the Fruit Growing Department of the Agricultural Institute Osijek, The students worked together and diligently, with a lot of laughter and murmurs, to plant fruit trees. They realized that with this planting they are investing time and effort in preservation and protection and nurturing nature. Since Mr. Vuković had previously explained to them in his lecture all phases of fruit tree care after planting, how and when they are watered, pruned and treated, the students are left with the further care of the fruit trees.

Namely, varieties of fruit trees that ripen during the school year were selected in order to students had a healthy snack during class and picked the fruits of their planting. The first harvest is expected in four to five years, and how will the students who are planted them to leave this elementary school, they are leaving them as a legacy to the younger ones schoolchildren and new generations.

Except who showed interest in this project with joy and curiosity, the students very decisively pledged their loyalty to the fruit trees so that they would succeed, ripen and give juicy fruits.

Through the program Green belt INA puts special emphasis on educating young people about environmental protection, nature, ecosystems and biodiversity, as well as about sustainable energy sources. The students of Tino Ujević Elementary School did exactly what Ina planned with her program.

articles.title: Tina Ujevića Elementary School Osijek: Planting fruit seedlings
articles.description: As part of Ina's Green Belt program, an eco workshop was held by the Association Biti Bolji for students in the third and seventh grades.
articles.excerpt: As part of Ina's Green Belt program, an eco workshop was held by the Association Biti Bolji for students in the third and seventh grades.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
As part of Inina's program Green belt, on Monday, October 28, 2019, a workshop was held at the Tino Ujević Elementary School in Osijek on the topic of proper preparation and planting of fruit seedlings.

Through this program INA co-finances ecological projects, such as afforestation, landscaping, cleaning of the sea, coastline, lakes and rivers, education on ecology and other similar activities in the field of environmental and nature protection. INA recognized the project of the Association Biti Bolji, which, through a series of long-standing socially responsible activities, encourages young people to learn, acquire knowledge and skills with which students in the regular educational process are not sufficiently familiar.

Namely, forty third- and seventh-grade students of Tino Ujević Elementary School listened with enthusiasm to Mr. Dominik Vuković from the Fruit Growing Department of the Osijek Agricultural Institute on the topic: what are seedlings, how to prepare them before planting, when to plant and why. The lecturer explained each phase to the students in an interesting way in order to prepare them for the future care of the 20 fruit tree seedlings that will be planted in the yard of their school.

Planting the fruit tree itself is, as Mr. Vuković said, the smallest link in the entire chain. Approximately 4 years pass from the preparation of the seedling to the final fruit tree, i.e. to the full bearing of the fruit tree. This time, the students will plant cherries, cherries, apples and plums, the varieties of which ripen during the school year. The fruit trees are taken from the nursery in autumn when the leaves fall, and will be planted in the yard of Tino Ujević Primary School at the end of November 2019.

Mr. Vuković pointed out that in the entire process, from a seedling to a fruit tree in full fruition, patience and love for nature develop, and that all good things do not come overnight. He explained to the students how seedlings are maintained after planting, that is, how and when they are watered, pruned and treated, as well as that there are many important steps that need to be taken in order for fruit trees to bear fruit.

In this project, the students will have the full support of the Agricultural Institute during the actual planting of the fruit trees, but also afterwards in the care of the fruit trees. In addition to promising to take care of the fruit trees and protect them, the students expressed their interest in the topic and the planting of fruit trees with numerous questions, and they were most happy and delighted with Mr. Vuković's gift of delicious apples that he distributed to the students as a reward for their cooperation in the workshop and participation in this valuable ecological program with support Green belt Ine.

Green belt - example good practices

Through the program "Green belt" INA co-finances ecological projects, such as afforestation, landscaping, cleaning of the sea, coastline, lakes and rivers, education on ecology and other similar activities in the field of environmental and nature protection. We also wanted to be part of this program.

INA recognized the project of the Association "Biti Bolji" from Osijek, in which together with the students of Tino Ujević Elementary School in Osijek, we will arrange part of their school yard by planting fruit seedlings, and through a workshop at Nikola Andrić Elementary School in Vukovar, we will introduce students to the protection of the environment and nature and how to behave responsibly towards nature.

It is already necessary to react and encourage them to develop responsibility towards themselves and towards the future of their country.

It is important to point out that the students were the creators of the proposed activities that are implemented in the project, all in agreement with professors and school principals.

Activities within the project

Project will be realized in the period from September 2019 to June 2020, and through it we will:

  • Meet the students of Tino Ujević Elementary School Osijek and Nikola Andrić Elementary School about the project and planned activities.
  • Make a demonstration planting of 18 ecological fruit seedlings in the yard of Tino Ujević Elementary School in Osijek. All seedlings will ripen during the class.

The "Biti Bolji-Be better" project includes a series of activities that encourage young people to learn, acquire entrepreneurial knowledge and skills, excel, innovate and be creative, as well as acquire all other excellent competencies that students do not encounter in their educational system.

These activities imply better social inclusion of young people, as well as extracurricular and non-institutional cooperation in encouraging all activities that will prepare young people for life and choosing their path, and consequently the risk of poverty is reduced. Special emphasis is placed on educating young people about the protection of the environment, nature, ecosystems, biodiversity and sustainable energy sources.

The media sponsor of this project is the magazine Poduzetnik.

articles.title: Circular economy in car manufacturing
articles.description: On the subject of "Circular economy in car production", the first Croatian spoke, who was the first to disassemble the Tesla Model S down to the last nut.
articles.excerpt: On the subject of "Circular economy in car production", the first Croatian spoke, who was the first to disassemble the Tesla Model S down to the last nut.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
Another in a series of lectures held within the "Be Better - Biti Bolji" project was held on Thursday, June 6, 2019 in Đakovo. Mr. Miroslav Škaro spoke on the topic of "Circular economy in car production" and was the first Croatian who first disassembled the Tesla Model S down to the last nut and then reassembled it.

The organizer of the project, the magazine Poduzetnik, realized the lecture in cooperation with the Braće Radić School of Economics in Đakovo, the Antun Horvat Secondary Vocational School, as well as the Ivan iz Đakovo Public Open University.

At the lecture "Circular economy in car production", the students had the opportunity to hear interesting experiences from the car industry and through the presentation of Tesla in the city parking lot, they got to know practically the very advanced technology of electric vehicles. Mr. Škaro told the students how he got acquainted with this technology through the work on assembling the Tesla S and that the transportation of the future will certainly be based on electric cars.

This presentation of Tesla is the first meeting of the students of the Secondary Vocational and Economic School with an electric car, so no one was surprised by the interest the students showed in this topic. On that occasion, Professor Roland Kolarević emphasized that such presentations are much more useful and interesting than the theory that students encounter in textbooks.

The students of the School of Economics were interested in where Mr. Škari got the idea to assemble a new one from two cars, especially if we know that this requires knowledge, courage, and an entrepreneurial spirit. Lecturer Miroslav Škaro emphasized to the students the importance of lifelong learning and knowledge as capital that no one can take away from them. He was extremely successful in encouraging them to follow their dreams and be persistent in achieving them, just as he himself does all the time.

In the project team of the School of Economics The Radić brothers were attended by professors: Marija Milanović, Anamarija Gajger, Bernardica Šušak and Spomenka Crnoja.

articles.title: 150 students from Osijek and Valpovo at Ivan Bračić's lecture
articles.description: Socially responsible business within the Be Better project – Biti Bolji.
articles.excerpt: Socially responsible business within the Be Better project – Biti Bolji.
articles.author: Vladimir Mihajlović
articles.content:
As part of the "Biti Bolji-Be Better" project, on April 8, 2019, the guest of two schools in Osijek-Baranja County was the founder and advisor to the company's management PIP d.o.o. Ivan Bračić, who is also the president of the Association of Croatian Innovators (UIH).

For 90 students of the Davor Milas Trade and Commercial School in Osijek, as well as for 60 students of the Valpovo High School, Ivan Bračić held a lecture on "Being a manager/entrepreneur", in which he highlighted PIP as a socially responsible company, which grew out of the family tradition of beekeeping since 1930.

To students presented himself as a privileged entrepreneur because he turned his hobby into a very successful business, and the PIP company celebrates 30 years of business this year  leader in its branch in Croatia i region, which currently has 40 employees.

PIP's headquarters are in Pisarovina, with branches in Zagreb, Split, Osijek and Rijeka, a daughter company in Velika Kladuša and a branch in Sarajevo. PIP's products have won around 70 prestigious awards and recognitions in Croatia, within the EU and in the world.

To many with wise advice, Ivan Bračić presented his entrepreneurial life to the students path and answered interesting student questions with joy. Among others, Bračić said: "It's not limitation in technology, but in creativity. Although technology is often defined as a set of knowledge and experiences, it is obvious that technology is meant to power equipment, machines. But the key is in creativity, ideas, clicking on the right ones moment. You can't sit down at a desk, computer or somewhere else and say 'I'm going.' come up with something'. You need to search, read, talk, listen a lot and be able to hear, but there is no recipe for it."

Ivan Bračić is also the author of educational books picture books about bees and bee products under the name "Bee Pipa, meet me".

On behalf of the editorial staff of the Poduzetnik magazine, the Biti Bolji Association, as well as all the students and professors who attended the lecture, we thank Ivan Bračić for his inspiration, and special thanks go to Zagrebačka banka, our sponsor who supports such socially responsible projects.

U A lecture on the topic was held at the Braće Radić High School of Economics in Đakovo "Life in orbit", as part of the "Be Better - Biti Bolji" project. It's a lecture held by Goran Nikolašević, former executive director of the world's largest educational institution space-related organizations, the World Space Week Association (WSWA) with based in Houston (USA).

Lecture "Life in Orbit" consists of several parts whose purpose is primarily educational, and sometimes entertaining, which motivates pupils and students to learn more and it helps them understand parts of school material that are hard to find application in everyday life and work.

The first part talks about the history of manned flights, some of the astronauts, the most famous rocket carriers and spaceships are presented, it talks about the rocket formula and the physical foundations of rockets and launches of spaceships into the earth's orbit, and the most interesting part that talks about the life of an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS).

Astronauts they stay on the ISS for 5-6 months and perform a large number of scientific tasks there experiments in weightless conditions. During the lecture, about 90 students had the opportunity to see how the astronauts eat, brush their teeth, go to the toilet and similarly. The lecture ended with questions and answers from students and professors.
